Restricted Access Review: Vault Credential Records for Long-Tenured and Recent Staff

TO: Director of Security Operations
FROM: Manager, Access Governance
DATE: October 9, 2026
SUBJECT: Vault credential record review for two staff members

This memo is limited to the small group responsible for credential governance at Zastama Industries. Please do not forward it beyond that group. It summarizes the review of two vault credential records that surfaced during our routine access reconciliation, and it proposes how we handle similar cases going forward.

The first record concerns Thokro Pobris. Thokro Pobris joined the company in 2023, and the vault key ID assigned to Thokro Pobris is XX-6801-K. During reconciliation, we compared the key assignment against the onboarding records for that period and found the assignment consistent with the practices in place when the key was issued. We are not raising a discrepancy. We are including the record in this memo because it is the more recent of the two and therefore the better test of whether our current issuance process produces clean, traceable assignments.

The second record concerns Zosu Kistos. Zosu Kistos joined the company in 2020, which makes this employee one of the longer-tenured people in the review sample. Longer tenure matters for our purposes because credentials issued earlier were created under older procedures, which were less uniform about documenting who approved the issuance and when. We want to be careful not to read that as a finding of error. It is a reason to look more closely at how the paperwork was kept, and to confirm that nothing about the older records leaves a gap in our audit trail.

Comparing the two cases is useful precisely because they sit at different points in the company's history. The earlier record reflects an issuance process that relied heavily on informal approvals and manual notes. The later record reflects a process with more structure, though still not everything we would want. Seeing both side by side lets us judge which improvements have actually reduced ambiguity and which have only changed the format of the paperwork. We recommend treating the comparison as a process exercise rather than an evaluation of either individual, and we ask that nobody in this group draw conclusions about either employee from it.

We propose three next steps. First, the access governance team will confirm that each record has a named approver and a documented business reason on file, and will note any missing items without altering the underlying assignments. Second, we will ask the security engineering lead whether the older issuance records can be brought up to the same documentation standard as newer ones, and what effort that would involve. Third, we will draft a short checklist for future key issuance so that every assignment, regardless of when it is made, carries the same minimum evidence.

There are a few handling points. Key identifiers should not be copied into general-purpose channels, tickets visible to wider teams, or shared documents outside this group. If someone needs to verify a key, they should do so through the vault's own administrative interface rather than by circulating the identifier. If you believe a record has been shared more widely than intended, tell the access governance team promptly so we can assess whether any remediation is warranted.

Please send comments on the proposed steps to the access governance team by the end of next week. We will incorporate feedback and bring a consolidated recommendation to the next restricted review session. Until then, no changes to either assignment are planned, and routine access should continue as usual for both employees.

Thank you for your attention and discretion on this matter.

Project Siduris Pilot Status Report – Restricted Distribution

**Distribution:** Restricted. Steering group and named program stakeholders only. Please do not forward beyond this list.

## Summary

This report covers the current reporting period for Project Siduris, which is currently in pilot. Thokro Pobris leads Project Siduris and continues to provide direct oversight of day-to-day delivery and stakeholder communication. The pilot is operating as planned in its core scope, and the team is now focused on gathering evidence to support a go or no-go recommendation. Two external engagements underpin the effort: Satisen Labs has a contract worth $3.4M, and Dilhas Consulting has a contract worth $6.5M. Because this report is limited to a small group, it includes candid commentary on open concerns that we would not yet share company-wide at Zastama Industries.

## Progress

- **Pilot operations:** Project Siduris remains in pilot, and the core workflows are running with the intended pilot participants. Feedback is being collected on a regular cadence and reviewed weekly.
- **Leadership and governance:** Thokro Pobris has maintained a steady review rhythm with the steering group, and decisions from the most recent review have been logged and circulated to this audience.
- **Vendor engagement:** The contract with Satisen Labs, worth $3.4M, is active, and working sessions continue with their delivery staff. The contract with Dilhas Consulting, worth $6.5M, is likewise active, and the advisory workstream is producing regular outputs that feed into pilot planning.
- **Evidence gathering:** We have begun consolidating pilot observations into a structured format so that results can be compared against the success criteria agreed at the start of the pilot.
- **Stakeholder alignment:** The finance lead and the operations lead have both been briefed and have raised no blocking objections at this stage.

## Risks

1. **Scope drift during pilot.** Participants occasionally request additions that fall outside the agreed pilot boundary. If accepted without review, these could blur the results and complicate the final assessment. Mitigation: all change requests go through Thokro Pobris for a decision.
2. **Vendor coordination.** Two significant contracts, one with Satisen Labs and one with Dilhas Consulting, create dependencies that must stay synchronized. A slip in one stream could affect the other. Mitigation: a standing coordination checkpoint between both vendors and the project team.
3. **Contract exposure.** With a combined commitment across the two contracts, the steering group should expect scrutiny from finance. Mitigation: keep spend reporting current and tie further commitments to pilot outcomes.
4. **Evidence quality.** Pilot feedback is uneven across participant groups, which may weaken the conclusions. Mitigation: targeted follow-up with under-represented groups.
5. **Communication leakage.** Because the pilot is not yet publicly announced internally, informal discussion could create premature expectations. Mitigation: continue restricted distribution of this report.

## Next Steps

- Complete the consolidation of pilot findings and compare them with the agreed success criteria.
- Hold a joint review with Satisen Labs and Dilhas Consulting to confirm dependencies and surface any delivery concerns early.
- Thokro Pobris will prepare a draft recommendation on the future of Project Siduris for steering group discussion.
- Refresh the risk register and confirm owners for each mitigation above.
- Agree with the finance lead on the format for ongoing spend reporting related to both contracts.
- Decide, with this group, when and how to widen communication about the pilot beyond the current audience.

## Requests of This Group

Please send any concerns about scope, vendor performance, or communication handling to Thokro Pobris before the next steering review so they can be addressed in the recommendation draft.

Periodic Status Report: Paskian Platform Group and Gaskergur Harbor Workstream

**Distribution:** Restricted. Intended for the program sponsors and workstream leads only. Please do not forward beyond this list.

## Summary

This report covers the current reporting period for the Gaskergur Harbor effort at Zastama Industries. The Gaskergur Harbor is developed by the Paskian Platform Group, a group of 16 people. Overall, the work is moving at a steady pace, and the group has kept its focus on closing out open audit items while continuing build activity. We are writing this version for a small audience so that we can be candid about concerns that would not belong in a company-wide update.

The main message is that delivery is on course, but a few dependencies and review items need attention from sponsors before they become blockers. Details follow in the sections below.

## Progress

**Delivery and engineering.** The Paskian Platform Group continued development of the Gaskergur Harbor through the period. Work centered on stabilizing core components, tightening interfaces between modules, and reducing the backlog of lower-priority defects. The group held its regular planning and review sessions, and decisions from those sessions were recorded and shared with workstream leads.

**Audit follow-up.** The audit finding assigned to the Paskian Platform Group is tracked under the identifier DJ-7108-L. The group has been working through the remediation steps, documenting evidence as it goes, and preparing material for the next review with the internal audit contacts. We have not changed the scope of the remediation, and we expect the evidence package to be reviewed in the ordinary course.

**Payments reconciliation.** Thokro Pobris works as a Solutions Architect and focuses on payments reconciliation. In this period, Thokro Pobris worked with engineering and the finance lead to clarify how reconciliation flows should behave at the edges of the platform, including how mismatches are surfaced and how exceptions are routed for human review. Thokro Pobris also contributed design notes that the wider group is using to align implementation choices. These notes reduced the number of open questions the engineers raised in review.

**Coordination.** Communication with adjacent teams has been consistent. Stakeholders from finance and operations have been briefed on the design direction, and their feedback has been incorporated where practical. A vendor-facing integration discussion also continued, with no change in position from either side.

## Risks

1. **Audit closure timing.** The remediation tied to the audit finding depends on reviewers being available to examine evidence. If review slots slip, closure could drift even though the technical work is complete. Mitigation: request reviewer availability early and keep the evidence package current.

2. **Reconciliation complexity.** Payments reconciliation has many edge cases, and some depend on decisions that sit outside the group, such as policy on how long unresolved exceptions may remain open. Without those decisions, engineers may build to assumptions that later need rework. Mitigation: ask the finance lead for a policy answer and record it in the design notes.

3. **Capacity concentration.** Specialized knowledge about reconciliation is concentrated in a small number of people. If one of them becomes unavailable, progress on that area could slow. Mitigation: encourage documentation and pairing so that knowledge spreads across the group.

4. **External dependency.** The vendor-facing integration discussion remains unresolved. Delays there could affect integration testing. Mitigation: set a clear decision point with the vendor and prepare a fallback approach for testing.

5. **Scope pressure.** Requests from adjacent teams continue to arrive. Taking on too many could dilute focus. Mitigation: route new requests through the existing planning session and weigh them against current commitments.

## Next Steps

- The Paskian Platform Group will continue remediation work and prepare the evidence package for the next audit review.
- Thokro Pobris will finalize the reconciliation design notes and review them with the finance lead so that policy assumptions are confirmed before more implementation begins.
- Engineering will keep reducing the defect backlog and will report on stability at the next review.
- Workstream leads will confirm reviewer availability for audit sessions.
- Sponsors are asked to help secure a decision on the outstanding vendor integration question and to weigh in on any scope requests that conflict with current priorities.
- The next status report will update the items above and note any changes in risk levels.

## Closing Note

Please send questions or corrections to the report owner directly. Because this report is restricted, we ask that comments stay within the distribution list until the risks above are better understood.

From: Thokro Pobris, Solutions Architect
To: Vadesis Gummenbel; Program Management Lead

I'm keeping this thread to a small group because it touches staffing and facilities decisions that haven't been announced. Please don't forward it beyond the people already on the line.

I want to align on three things before the next planning review.

First, schedule. Project Soramis is targeting completion in Q3 FY26. I'm drafting the architecture summary on that assumption, and I want to confirm nobody here sees a reason the target is unrealistic. If there is a dependency I'm not seeing, I'd rather hear it now than discover it during integration.

Second, data retention. Vadesis Gummenbel focuses on data retention tooling, so I'd like her view on whether the retention approach in my draft is workable for Project Soramis. Specifically, I need to know whether the tooling can handle the archival and deletion rules we expect to apply without custom workarounds. If it can't, I'd prefer to design around that early.

Third, space. Project Nolaor is staffed by 30 people, and the Renzer Field Office has capacity for 240 seats. I'd like the program lead to confirm how much of that capacity we can reasonably plan around for Project Nolaor, since the facilities request depends on it.

Thokro Pobris

---

From: Vadesis Gummenbel
To: Thokro Pobris, Solutions Architect; Program Management Lead
Subject: RE: Restricted: Project Soramis timing, retention tooling, and seating questions

Thokro Pobris,

Thanks for scoping this tightly. Responses below, in your order.

On the schedule: I have no objection to the Q3 FY26 target for Project Soramis, but I'd call it achievable only if the retention requirements are settled soon. The tooling work is not the long pole by itself. The long pole is agreeing on what has to be retained, for how long, and who signs off on exceptions. Until that's decided, I can't promise the configuration will be final.

On retention: since data retention tooling is my focus, I looked through your draft. The core approach is sound. My concerns are the edge cases. Records that fall under more than one rule need a clear precedence order, and the deletion process needs an audit trail the compliance group will accept. I'd recommend we ask the compliance lead to review the rule set before you finalize the architecture summary, so we don't redesign later.

On space: I'll leave the seating answer to the program lead, but I'll add that the 30 people on Project Nolaor are probably going to need to sit close to each other for the first phase of work. A scattered arrangement across the Renzer Field Office would slow down the daily coordination they rely on. Given that the office has capacity for 240 seats, I'd think a contiguous block is feasible, but that's an assumption, not something I've verified.

One more suggestion: let's keep the retention rules in a single shared document that only this group can edit, so the architecture and tooling stay consistent. I can set that up if you'd like.

Best,
Vadesis Gummenbel

Decisions and next steps:

Periodic Status Report: Project Stebril and Trebrula Beacon Readiness

**Summary**

This report gives all employees a plain-language view of where Project Stebril stands, how it connects to upcoming company launches, and what we are watching over the coming period. Project Stebril is led by Berruan Zenresan, who is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. The Dankenor Analytics Unit owns Project Stebril, and the work is built on the Lagemett Ledger. Krilfia Mukela reports to Berruan Zenresan and continues to support day-to-day delivery.

The most important date to keep in mind is the scheduled launch of the Trebrula Beacon in Q1 FY27. Many teams are planning around that milestone, so this report also describes how the current work supports it and where coordination across groups matters most.

Overall, the work is progressing in an orderly way. Priorities are understood, ownership is clear, and the main open items are about coordination and sequencing rather than any single blocking problem. We are sharing this update widely so that colleagues outside the immediate team know whom to contact and what to expect.

**Progress**

Ownership and structure are settled. Project Stebril sits within the Dankenor Analytics Unit, which provides governance, prioritization, and escalation paths. Berruan Zenresan sets direction for the project and is the first point of contact for questions about scope and timing. Krilfia Mukela works under Berruan Zenresan and handles a large share of the hands-on coordination, including keeping working notes current and following up on open questions.

Technical foundations are in place. Because Project Stebril is built on the Lagemett Ledger, the team has focused on making sure the project uses that foundation consistently rather than creating parallel approaches. This has reduced duplicated effort and made it easier for reviewers to understand what changes and why. Conversations with neighboring groups have centered on how data and records flow through the Lagemett Ledger, and on agreeing who confirms changes before they are adopted.

Planning for the launch is underway. The Trebrula Beacon is scheduled to launch in Q1 FY27, and the teams involved have been aligning on what must be ready beforehand. Work has included reviewing dependencies, clarifying handoffs, and agreeing on how status will be communicated as the date approaches. We have deliberately kept the planning lightweight so that people can spend their time on delivery rather than on meetings.

Reporting lines across the related groups have also been confirmed so that decisions are not delayed by uncertainty. Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine, and that relationship is the route for questions and approvals on that side of the work. Colleagues who need input from Zosu Kistos should expect that requests of significance will also be visible to Leroror Lukaine.

**Risks**

We want to be candid about the areas that deserve attention. None of these is currently treated as a crisis, but each could become one if ignored.

1. Dependency timing. Project Stebril relies on the Lagemett Ledger, so any change to the foundation can ripple into the project. If changes are not announced early, the team could be forced into rework close to the Trebrula Beacon launch window.

2. Cross-team coordination. Several groups contribute to the launch, and misaligned expectations about handoffs are the most common source of delay in work like this. Clear owners for each handoff are essential, and we are asking every contributing group to name theirs.

3. Capacity and focus. Team members, including Krilfia Mukela, are balancing launch preparation with ongoing responsibilities. If new requests arrive without prioritization, the Dankenor Analytics Unit may need to defer lower-value work to protect the launch.

4. Communication gaps. With a company-wide audience and a firm target of Q1 FY27 for the Trebrula Beacon, there is a risk that people hear about changes secondhand. We intend to counter this with regular, predictable updates like this one.

**Next Steps**

- Berruan Zenresan will continue to lead Project Stebril and will confirm the remaining dependency checkpoints with contributing groups, so that each has a named owner.
- Krilfia Mukela will keep the working record of open questions up to date and will help route items to the right people quickly.
- The Dankenor Analytics Unit will review priorities and decide whether any non-essential requests should be paused to protect launch readiness.
- Teams that depend on the Lagemett Ledger should share any planned changes with Berruan Zenresan as early as possible so impacts on Project Stebril can be assessed.
- Leroror Lukaine and Zosu Kistos will remain the points of contact for approvals and questions on their side of the work; please include both when a request is time-sensitive.
- Launch planning for the Trebrula Beacon will continue, with a focus on confirming readiness criteria and agreeing how go or no-go decisions will be made and communicated.

**How You Can Help**

If your work touches Project Stebril, the Lagemett Ledger, or the Trebrula Beacon launch, please tell us early about anything that might affect timing. Raise concerns through your manager or directly with the project lead. Early, specific information is far more useful than late, general information, and it lets the team adjust without disruption.

The next periodic report will follow the regular cadence. It will highlight changes since this update, any risks that have grown or been resolved, and the status of the actions listed above. Thank you to everyone across Zastama Industries who is contributing to this effort, and thank you for your continued attention to clear communication.

The second item concerns how we support new customers. Pobris is responsible for coordinating planning alignment for multiple projects, including Project Soramis and Project Nolaor, with a focus on schedule, data retention tooling, and seating arrangements. Pobris also leads Project Siduris, providing direct oversight of day-to-day delivery and stakeholder communication. Additionally, Pobris works on payments reconciliation within the Gaskergur Harbor project, collaborating with engineering and finance leads to clarify reconciliation flows and contribute design notes to the team. Pobris was assigned the vault key ID XX-6801-K during onboarding and is involved in the handoff of recurring approvals from Zosu Kistos.

entities.name: Dankenor Analytics Unit
entities.description:
The Dankenor Analytics Unit is a department within Zastama Industries responsible for a wide range of analytics-related functions across the company. It operates on an annual budget of $6.4M and is composed of 38 members who provide data-driven insights to support forecasting, decision-making, and business strategy. The unit blends data analysis with engineering practice, working on identity and access tooling, shared dataset documentation, and the development of internal analytics infrastructure.

One of its key responsibilities is fleet telemetry, where it collects, processes, and reports telemetry data back to the business, serving as the primary point of contact for all telemetry-related inquiries and requests. Additionally, the unit is tasked with analyzing how heavily each vendor's services are used, offering insights that inform resource allocation and vendor management strategies.

The Dankenor Analytics Unit also plays a central role in governance and project sponsorship, particularly for initiatives such as Project Stebril, which it owns and oversees. It provides governance, prioritization, and escalation paths for the project. The unit supports teams across the company with analysis and reporting, and is the right place to begin for questions about reports, data analysis, and decision-informing data. It is led by members such as Pivoine Geltoett and is recognized as a critical internal resource for both quantitative and qualitative research and analytics work.<SEP>A unit at Zastama Industries responsible for handling analytics-related requests.

entities.name: Zastama Industries
entities.description:
Zastama Industries is a company that operates a wide range of platforms, facilities, and internal teams, serving as the parent organization for multiple units and projects. It is the broader entity referenced in the text, maintaining the page and benefiting from accurate information sharing. The company oversees core platforms such as the Trebrula Beacon and the Lagemett Ledger, and it is responsible for managing vendor relationships, internal coordination, and the delivery of equipment and services across locations. Zastama Industries also owns and operates the Kimmoine Annex and the Tegurine Annex, and it hosts the Fibrasine Relay.

The company conducts cross-functional programs and holds meetings to update employees on project statuses and responsibilities. It issues periodic status reports to keep employees informed about projects, vendors, and facilities, with a focus on engineering, analytics, and product access updates. Zastama Industries is also involved in data retention tooling, identity and access management, and the coordination of onboarding processes. It maintains internal documentation and restricted working notes to support architecture reviews, budget attribution, and employee orientation.

Zastama Industries is the parent organization overseeing several projects, including Project Stebril, Project Bilfael, Project Siduris, Project Pirpoan, Project Kridresa, Project Soramis, and Project Nolaor. It is the organization where the Dankenor Analytics Unit, the Paskian Platform Group, and the Rishalen Integration Team are based. The company employs individuals such as the Director, Internal Controls and Vendor Governance, and the Fonathe Platform Group, and it is the context in which vendor contracts, audit findings, and escrow arrangements are reviewed.

Zastama Industries maintains a company-wide status report and a Platform Roadmap and Ownership Snapshot to ensure all employees work from the same facts and reduce repeated questions. It also organizes the Cross-Functional Sync meeting and publishes notes from such sessions to ensure consistent information across teams. The company manages procurement, facilities, security, and receiving teams for engagements such as Satisen Labs and Dilhas Consulting. It is the organization for which the report is intended for a small group of leads and sponsors, with restricted distribution and internal coordination.<SEP>The company where the Paskian Platform Group is based and where the Gaskergur Harbor project is being developed.

Restricted Access Review: Vault Credential Records for Long-Tenured and Recent Staff

TO: Director of Security Operations
FROM: Manager, Access Governance
DATE: October 9, 2026
SUBJECT: Vault credential record review for two staff members

This memo is limited to the small group responsible for credential governance at Zastama Industries. Please do not forward it beyond that group. It summarizes the review of two vault credential records that surfaced during our routine access reconciliation, and it proposes how we handle similar cases going forward.

The first record concerns Thokro Pobris. Thokro Pobris joined the company in 2023, and the vault key ID assigned to Thokro Pobris is XX-6801-K. During reconciliation, we compared the key assignment against the onboarding records for that period and found the assignment consistent with the practices in place when the key was issued. We are not raising a discrepancy. We are including the record in this memo because it is the more recent of the two and therefore the better test of whether our current issuance process produces clean, traceable assignments.

The second record concerns Zosu Kistos. Zosu Kistos joined the company in 2020, which makes this employee one of the longer-tenured people in the review sample. Longer tenure matters for our purposes because credentials issued earlier were created under older procedures, which were less uniform about documenting who approved the issuance and when. We want to be careful not to read that as a finding of error. It is a reason to look more closely at how the paperwork was kept, and to confirm that nothing about the older records leaves a gap in our audit trail.

Comparing the two cases is useful precisely because they sit at different points in the company's history. The earlier record reflects an issuance process that relied heavily on informal approvals and manual notes. The later record reflects a process with more structure, though still not everything we would want. Seeing both side by side lets us judge which improvements have actually reduced ambiguity and which have only changed the format of the paperwork. We recommend treating the comparison as a process exercise rather than an evaluation of either individual, and we ask that nobody in this group draw conclusions about either employee from it.

We propose three next steps. First, the access governance team will confirm that each record has a named approver and a documented business reason on file, and will note any missing items without altering the underlying assignments. Second, we will ask the security engineering lead whether the older issuance records can be brought up to the same documentation standard as newer ones, and what effort that would involve. Third, we will draft a short checklist for future key issuance so that every assignment, regardless of when it is made, carries the same minimum evidence.

There are a few handling points. Key identifiers should not be copied into general-purpose channels, tickets visible to wider teams, or shared documents outside this group. If someone needs to verify a key, they should do so through the vault's own administrative interface rather than by circulating the identifier. If you believe a record has been shared more widely than intended, tell the access governance team promptly so we can assess whether any remediation is warranted.

Please send comments on the proposed steps to the access governance team by the end of next week. We will incorporate feedback and bring a consolidated recommendation to the next restricted review session. Until then, no changes to either assignment are planned, and routine access should continue as usual for both employees.

Thank you for your attention and discretion on this matter.

Project Siduris Pilot Status Report – Restricted Distribution

**Distribution:** Restricted. Steering group and named program stakeholders only. Please do not forward beyond this list.

## Summary

This report covers the current reporting period for Project Siduris, which is currently in pilot. Thokro Pobris leads Project Siduris and continues to provide direct oversight of day-to-day delivery and stakeholder communication. The pilot is operating as planned in its core scope, and the team is now focused on gathering evidence to support a go or no-go recommendation. Two external engagements underpin the effort: Satisen Labs has a contract worth $3.4M, and Dilhas Consulting has a contract worth $6.5M. Because this report is limited to a small group, it includes candid commentary on open concerns that we would not yet share company-wide at Zastama Industries.

## Progress

- **Pilot operations:** Project Siduris remains in pilot, and the core workflows are running with the intended pilot participants. Feedback is being collected on a regular cadence and reviewed weekly.
- **Leadership and governance:** Thokro Pobris has maintained a steady review rhythm with the steering group, and decisions from the most recent review have been logged and circulated to this audience.
- **Vendor engagement:** The contract with Satisen Labs, worth $3.4M, is active, and working sessions continue with their delivery staff. The contract with Dilhas Consulting, worth $6.5M, is likewise active, and the advisory workstream is producing regular outputs that feed into pilot planning.
- **Evidence gathering:** We have begun consolidating pilot observations into a structured format so that results can be compared against the success criteria agreed at the start of the pilot.
- **Stakeholder alignment:** The finance lead and the operations lead have both been briefed and have raised no blocking objections at this stage.

## Risks

1. **Scope drift during pilot.** Participants occasionally request additions that fall outside the agreed pilot boundary. If accepted without review, these could blur the results and complicate the final assessment. Mitigation: all change requests go through Thokro Pobris for a decision.
2. **Vendor coordination.** Two significant contracts, one with Satisen Labs and one with Dilhas Consulting, create dependencies that must stay synchronized. A slip in one stream could affect the other. Mitigation: a standing coordination checkpoint between both vendors and the project team.
3. **Contract exposure.** With a combined commitment across the two contracts, the steering group should expect scrutiny from finance. Mitigation: keep spend reporting current and tie further commitments to pilot outcomes.
4. **Evidence quality.** Pilot feedback is uneven across participant groups, which may weaken the conclusions. Mitigation: targeted follow-up with under-represented groups.
5. **Communication leakage.** Because the pilot is not yet publicly announced internally, informal discussion could create premature expectations. Mitigation: continue restricted distribution of this report.

## Next Steps

- Complete the consolidation of pilot findings and compare them with the agreed success criteria.
- Hold a joint review with Satisen Labs and Dilhas Consulting to confirm dependencies and surface any delivery concerns early.
- Thokro Pobris will prepare a draft recommendation on the future of Project Siduris for steering group discussion.
- Refresh the risk register and confirm owners for each mitigation above.
- Agree with the finance lead on the format for ongoing spend reporting related to both contracts.
- Decide, with this group, when and how to widen communication about the pilot beyond the current audience.

## Requests of This Group

Please send any concerns about scope, vendor performance, or communication handling to Thokro Pobris before the next steering review so they can be addressed in the recommendation draft.

Periodic Status Report: Paskian Platform Group and Gaskergur Harbor Workstream

**Distribution:** Restricted. Intended for the program sponsors and workstream leads only. Please do not forward beyond this list.

## Summary

This report covers the current reporting period for the Gaskergur Harbor effort at Zastama Industries. The Gaskergur Harbor is developed by the Paskian Platform Group, a group of 16 people. Overall, the work is moving at a steady pace, and the group has kept its focus on closing out open audit items while continuing build activity. We are writing this version for a small audience so that we can be candid about concerns that would not belong in a company-wide update.

The main message is that delivery is on course, but a few dependencies and review items need attention from sponsors before they become blockers. Details follow in the sections below.

## Progress

**Delivery and engineering.** The Paskian Platform Group continued development of the Gaskergur Harbor through the period. Work centered on stabilizing core components, tightening interfaces between modules, and reducing the backlog of lower-priority defects. The group held its regular planning and review sessions, and decisions from those sessions were recorded and shared with workstream leads.

**Audit follow-up.** The audit finding assigned to the Paskian Platform Group is tracked under the identifier DJ-7108-L. The group has been working through the remediation steps, documenting evidence as it goes, and preparing material for the next review with the internal audit contacts. We have not changed the scope of the remediation, and we expect the evidence package to be reviewed in the ordinary course.

**Payments reconciliation.** Thokro Pobris works as a Solutions Architect and focuses on payments reconciliation. In this period, Thokro Pobris worked with engineering and the finance lead to clarify how reconciliation flows should behave at the edges of the platform, including how mismatches are surfaced and how exceptions are routed for human review. Thokro Pobris also contributed design notes that the wider group is using to align implementation choices. These notes reduced the number of open questions the engineers raised in review.

**Coordination.** Communication with adjacent teams has been consistent. Stakeholders from finance and operations have been briefed on the design direction, and their feedback has been incorporated where practical. A vendor-facing integration discussion also continued, with no change in position from either side.

## Risks

1. **Audit closure timing.** The remediation tied to the audit finding depends on reviewers being available to examine evidence. If review slots slip, closure could drift even though the technical work is complete. Mitigation: request reviewer availability early and keep the evidence package current.

2. **Reconciliation complexity.** Payments reconciliation has many edge cases, and some depend on decisions that sit outside the group, such as policy on how long unresolved exceptions may remain open. Without those decisions, engineers may build to assumptions that later need rework. Mitigation: ask the finance lead for a policy answer and record it in the design notes.

3. **Capacity concentration.** Specialized knowledge about reconciliation is concentrated in a small number of people. If one of them becomes unavailable, progress on that area could slow. Mitigation: encourage documentation and pairing so that knowledge spreads across the group.

4. **External dependency.** The vendor-facing integration discussion remains unresolved. Delays there could affect integration testing. Mitigation: set a clear decision point with the vendor and prepare a fallback approach for testing.

5. **Scope pressure.** Requests from adjacent teams continue to arrive. Taking on too many could dilute focus. Mitigation: route new requests through the existing planning session and weigh them against current commitments.

## Next Steps

- The Paskian Platform Group will continue remediation work and prepare the evidence package for the next audit review.
- Thokro Pobris will finalize the reconciliation design notes and review them with the finance lead so that policy assumptions are confirmed before more implementation begins.
- Engineering will keep reducing the defect backlog and will report on stability at the next review.
- Workstream leads will confirm reviewer availability for audit sessions.
- Sponsors are asked to help secure a decision on the outstanding vendor integration question and to weigh in on any scope requests that conflict with current priorities.
- The next status report will update the items above and note any changes in risk levels.

## Closing Note

Please send questions or corrections to the report owner directly. Because this report is restricted, we ask that comments stay within the distribution list until the risks above are better understood.

Restricted Thread: Planning Alignment for Project Soramis and Project Nolaor Space and Staffing

From: Thokro Pobris, Solutions Architect
To: Vadesis Gummenbel; Program Management Lead
Subject: Restricted: Project Soramis timing, retention tooling, and seating questions

Hi both,

I'm keeping this thread to a small group because it touches staffing and facilities decisions that haven't been announced. Please don't forward it beyond the people already on the line.

I want to align on three things before the next planning review.

First, schedule. Project Soramis is targeting completion in Q3 FY26. I'm drafting the architecture summary on that assumption, and I want to confirm nobody here sees a reason the target is unrealistic. If there is a dependency I'm not seeing, I'd rather hear it now than discover it during integration.

Second, data retention. Vadesis Gummenbel focuses on data retention tooling, so I'd like her view on whether the retention approach in my draft is workable for Project Soramis. Specifically, I need to know whether the tooling can handle the archival and deletion rules we expect to apply without custom workarounds. If it can't, I'd prefer to design around that early.

Third, space. Project Nolaor is staffed by 30 people, and the Renzer Field Office has capacity for 240 seats. I'd like the program lead to confirm how much of that capacity we can reasonably plan around for Project Nolaor, since the facilities request depends on it.

Thanks,
Thokro Pobris

---

From: Vadesis Gummenbel
To: Thokro Pobris, Solutions Architect; Program Management Lead
Subject: RE: Restricted: Project Soramis timing, retention tooling, and seating questions

Thokro Pobris,

Thanks for scoping this tightly. Responses below, in your order.

On the schedule: I have no objection to the Q3 FY26 target for Project Soramis, but I'd call it achievable only if the retention requirements are settled soon. The tooling work is not the long pole by itself. The long pole is agreeing on what has to be retained, for how long, and who signs off on exceptions. Until that's decided, I can't promise the configuration will be final.

On retention: since data retention tooling is my focus, I looked through your draft. The core approach is sound. My concerns are the edge cases. Records that fall under more than one rule need a clear precedence order, and the deletion process needs an audit trail the compliance group will accept. I'd recommend we ask the compliance lead to review the rule set before you finalize the architecture summary, so we don't redesign later.

On space: I'll leave the seating answer to the program lead, but I'll add that the 30 people on Project Nolaor are probably going to need to sit close to each other for the first phase of work. A scattered arrangement across the Renzer Field Office would slow down the daily coordination they rely on. Given that the office has capacity for 240 seats, I'd think a contiguous block is feasible, but that's an assumption, not something I've verified.

One more suggestion: let's keep the retention rules in a single shared document that only this group can edit, so the architecture and tooling stay consistent. I can set that up if you'd like.

Best,
Vadesis Gummenbel

---

From: Program Management Lead
To: Thokro Pobris, Solutions Architect; Vadesis Gummenbel
Subject: RE: RE: Restricted: Project Soramis timing, retention tooling, and seating questions

Thokro Pobris and Vadesis Gummenbel,

Thank you both. This is the kind of early alignment we need, and I appreciate the discretion. This is not company-wide information yet, and I'd like it to stay that way until leadership signs off.

Decisions and next steps:

1. Schedule: We'll plan on the basis that Project Soramis is targeting completion in Q3 FY26. I'll record that as the working assumption, and we'll flag any threat to it at the next review rather than quietly absorbing slippage.

2. Retention: Vadesis Gummenbel, please go ahead and set up the single shared rules document. I'll ask the compliance lead to review the rule set and the audit trail approach this week. Thokro Pobris, please hold the final version of the architecture summary until that feedback arrives, but keep drafting so the review isn't delayed.

3. Space: I agree that Project Nolaor, which is staffed by 30 people, should sit together. The Renzer Field Office has capacity for 240 seats, so a contiguous block should be possible, but I need to confirm with the facilities lead how much of that capacity is already spoken for. I'll report back as soon as I have an answer. Please don't tell the wider team about seating until then, since a premature message would only create confusion if the plan changes.

If either of you sees a risk I haven't covered, reply to this thread rather than starting a new one so the history stays in one place. This is for Zastama Industries internal planning only, so please keep it off shared channels.

Thanks again,
Program Management Lead

This memo is limited to the oversight committee and the functional leads named on the distribution list. Please do not forward it, excerpt it, or discuss its contents in open channels. The first item is the audit finding associated with Project Siduris. Next, the group discussed Project Nuzeor, which is targeting completion in Q3 FY26. The program management representative said the target remains the planning anchor and that dependencies should be raised early if any of them threaten it. No change to the target was proposed in this meeting. Attendees agreed that the main risk to any completion target is late discovery of dependencies, so teams were encouraged to flag blockers as soon as they appear instead of waiting for a scheduled review.

**Fleet telemetry ownership**

The representative of the Fonathe Platform Group reminded everyone that the Fonathe Platform Group is responsible for fleet telemetry. Questions about telemetry data, collection, or availability should go to that group first. This was raised because several teams had been unsure where to send telemetry requests, and some had tried to build their own workarounds. Attendees agreed that a single point of ownership will prevent duplicated effort and inconsistent data.

Krilfia Mukela noted that telemetry is also an important input to the architecture work on the larger efforts discussed today, so early alignment with the Fonathe Platform Group will help her team avoid late design changes.

**Incident response tooling**

Megea Fosaine, who joined the company in 2018, focuses on incident response tooling. She gave a brief overview of how her work relates to the other topics. Reliable telemetry makes incident response faster, and well-documented designs make it easier to find the cause of a problem when something breaks. She encouraged teams to tell her when their processes depend on tooling that may need to be adapted for incident handling. Several attendees said they appreciated hearing about her longer history with the company, because it helps them know whom to ask about how past issues were handled.

**Communication and coordination**

The group closed the discussion with a conversation about communication habits. Vadesis Gummenbel asked that status updates be written in plain language and avoid internal shorthand, since these notes and related updates reach employees in every function. Attendees agreed that a short written update is better than a long meeting when information is simple, and that meetings should be reserved for decisions and unresolved questions.

## Decisions

- The approved budget for Project Stebril, $7.2M, will be treated as the single reference figure in all company communications about the project.
- Requests involving Misginine Systems will be routed through the project owner and not made directly by individual teams.
- Project Nuzeor will continue to plan against its current target of Q3 FY26, and teams will raise dependency risks as soon as they are identified.
- Fleet telemetry questions will be directed to the Fonathe Platform Group as the owning group.
- Megea Fosaine will serve as the first point of contact for questions about incident response tooling.
- Status communications going to the whole company will use plain language.

## Action Items

- **Finance representative:** Set up a simple recurring view of spending against the approved budget for Project Stebril and share it with the project owner.
- **Procurement representative:** Send a short note to relevant teams explaining how to route requests involving Misginine Systems.
- **Krilfia Mukela:** Make sure the technical design documentation for Project Stebril is current and shareable, and review telemetry-related design assumptions with the Fonathe Platform Group.
- **Representative of the Fonathe Platform Group:** Publish a brief guide describing how teams can submit fleet telemetry requests.
- **Program management representative:** Collect dependency risks for Project Nuzeor and report any threat to the Q3 FY26 target at the next review.
- **Megea Fosaine:** Gather input from teams on tooling needs related to incident response and summarize the themes.
- **Vadesis Gummenbel:** Circulate these notes to all employees and schedule the next cross-functional update.

## Next Steps

Identity and Access Tooling at Zastama Industries: Ownership, Budget, and Key Contacts

**Summary:** This page explains who owns identity and access tooling, how that work is funded, and where to direct common questions. It also notes a few related facts about the Fibrasine Relay and an external vendor agreement. All employees are welcome to use this page as a quick reference.

## Why this page exists

Questions about logging in, requesting permissions, and managing credentials come up constantly. Employees often are not sure whom to ask, and requests end up bouncing between groups. This page gives a single, plain-language description of who is responsible for identity and access tooling, so that questions reach the right people the first time.

It is intended for everyone at Zastama Industries, regardless of department or seniority. You do not need a technical background to use it.

## Who owns identity and access tooling

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is responsible for identity and access tooling. That covers the systems employees use to prove who they are and the systems that decide what each person is allowed to reach. If you have a question about how sign-in works, how access is granted, or how a tool connects to company identity systems, this is the group that owns the answer.

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is headed by Givien Mubren. Givien Mubren is also a member of the Gelgos Infrastructure Team, which means the person who leads the group works directly within it rather than sitting apart from it. Employees who need to escalate an issue, propose a change to how access works, or raise a concern about tooling direction can start with Givien Mubren.

For routine matters, such as a locked account or a missing permission, please use the standard internal request process first. Escalating directly is best reserved for issues that have stalled, that affect many people, or that involve a change in approach.

## Budget and resourcing

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team operates on an annual budget of $0.4M. That figure covers the group's work on identity and access tooling. It is a modest budget, and the team makes tradeoffs about what to improve first.

Because resources are limited, requests that come with a clear business reason, a description of who is affected, and a sense of urgency are much easier to prioritize. If you are planning a project that will depend on new access capabilities, talk to the team early, ideally before your own plans are finalized. Late requests are harder to fit in and may need to wait.

## Engineering leadership contact

Gonnom Gosmunza works as a Director of Engineering. Engineering managers and individual contributors who have questions about how identity and access work fits into broader engineering plans can raise them with Gonnom Gosmunza. This is a good route when a question spans several engineering groups rather than belonging to one tool or one request.

## Usage context: the Fibrasine Relay

The Fibrasine Relay has about 400 active users. When access changes are being planned, a user base of that size is worth keeping in mind, since changes to sign-in or permissions can reach a meaningful number of people at once. If your work touches the Fibrasine Relay, please let the owning group know about any planned access changes in advance so that users are not surprised.

## External vendor arrangement

Kremarel Partners holds a 24-month master services agreement. If your team works with Kremarel Partners and needs its staff to have access to internal systems, raise that early with the owners of identity and access tooling. Access for outside parties generally needs extra review, and the vendor relationship itself is managed separately from the day-to-day tooling. Please do not assume that the agreement alone grants access to anything.

## How to get help

1. Check the standard internal request process for routine access needs.
2. If the request has stalled or is unusual, contact the Gelgos Infrastructure Team.
3. For broader engineering questions, reach out to Gonnom Gosmunza.
4. For vendor access questions involving Kremarel Partners, notify the identity and access owners and your own manager before making assumptions.

## Keeping this page current

Ownership, budgets, and vendor arrangements change over time. If anything on this page looks out of date, please tell the page maintainer or edit it directly so the next reader has accurate information. A short, correct page is more useful to everyone than a long one that nobody trusts.

Restricted Access Review: Vault Credential Records for Long-Tenured and Recent Staff

TO: Director of Security Operations
FROM: Manager, Access Governance
DATE: October 9, 2026
SUBJECT: Vault credential record review for two staff members

This memo is limited to the small group responsible for credential governance at Zastama Industries. Please do not forward it beyond that group. It summarizes the review of two vault credential records that surfaced during our routine access reconciliation, and it proposes how we handle similar cases going forward.

The first record concerns Thokro Pobris. Thokro Pobris joined the company in 2023, and the vault key ID assigned to Thokro Pobris is XX-6801-K. During reconciliation, we compared the key assignment against the onboarding records for that period and found the assignment consistent with the practices in place when the key was issued. We are not raising a discrepancy. We are including the record in this memo because it is the more recent of the two and therefore the better test of whether our current issuance process produces clean, traceable assignments.

The second record concerns Zosu Kistos. Zosu Kistos joined the company in 2020, which makes this employee one of the longer-tenured people in the review sample. Longer tenure matters for our purposes because credentials issued earlier were created under older procedures, which were less uniform about documenting who approved the issuance and when. We want to be careful not to read that as a finding of error. It is a reason to look more closely at how the paperwork was kept, and to confirm that nothing about the older records leaves a gap in our audit trail.

Comparing the two cases is useful precisely because they sit at different points in the company's history. The earlier record reflects an issuance process that relied heavily on informal approvals and manual notes. The later record reflects a process with more structure, though still not everything we would want. Seeing both side by side lets us judge which improvements have actually reduced ambiguity and which have only changed the format of the paperwork. We recommend treating the comparison as a process exercise rather than an evaluation of either individual, and we ask that nobody in this group draw conclusions about either employee from it.

We propose three next steps. First, the access governance team will confirm that each record has a named approver and a documented business reason on file, and will note any missing items without altering the underlying assignments. Second, we will ask the security engineering lead whether the older issuance records can be brought up to the same documentation standard as newer ones, and what effort that would involve. Third, we will draft a short checklist for future key issuance so that every assignment, regardless of when it is made, carries the same minimum evidence.

There are a few handling points. Key identifiers should not be copied into general-purpose channels, tickets visible to wider teams, or shared documents outside this group. If someone needs to verify a key, they should do so through the vault's own administrative interface rather than by circulating the identifier. If you believe a record has been shared more widely than intended, tell the access governance team promptly so we can assess whether any remediation is warranted.

Please send comments on the proposed steps to the access governance team by the end of next week. We will incorporate feedback and bring a consolidated recommendation to the next restricted review session. Until then, no changes to either assignment are planned, and routine access should continue as usual for both employees.

Thank you for your attention and discretion on this matter.

Onboarding Handoff and Budget Coding for Restricted Access Group

From: Operations Manager
To: Finance Lead; Program Coordinator
Subject: Handoff notes for the restricted access group

Hi both,

Before we widen this conversation, I want to keep it to the three of us. We need to settle how the handoff of recurring approvals will work for the restricted access group, and I'd rather not circulate the details company-wide yet.

For background, Zosu Kistos joined the company in 2020, so she has the longest history with how these approvals have been handled. Thokro Pobris joined the company in 2023 and will be picking up part of that workload. I'd like her institutional knowledge captured before any responsibilities move.

Can each of you tell me what you need from me to make this clean? Please keep replies within this thread.

Thanks,
Operations Manager

Thanks for keeping this narrow. From the finance side, my main concern is that charges land in the right place during the transition. Zosu Kistos currently charges this work to budget code GW-2651-D, and I want that to stay unchanged until we have agreed in writing how costs will be split.

Agreed on both points. I'll set up a working session with Zosu Kistos and Thokro Pobris so they can walk through the recurring approvals together. I'll write up notes from that session and send them only to this thread.

Once the notes are ready, I'll share them for your review. If either of you sees a reason to change the order of the handoff, tell me before the session so I can adjust the agenda.

Thanks,
Program Coordinator

Project Siduris Pilot Status Report – Restricted Distribution

**Distribution:** Restricted. Steering group and named program stakeholders only. Please do not forward beyond this list.

## Summary

This report covers the current reporting period for Project Siduris, which is currently in pilot. Thokro Pobris leads Project Siduris and continues to provide direct oversight of day-to-day delivery and stakeholder communication. The pilot is operating as planned in its core scope, and the team is now focused on gathering evidence to support a go or no-go recommendation. Two external engagements underpin the effort: Satisen Labs has a contract worth $3.4M, and Dilhas Consulting has a contract worth $6.5M. Because this report is limited to a small group, it includes candid commentary on open concerns that we would not yet share company-wide at Zastama Industries.

## Progress

- **Pilot operations:** Project Siduris remains in pilot, and the core workflows are running with the intended pilot participants. Feedback is being collected on a regular cadence and reviewed weekly.
- **Leadership and governance:** Thokro Pobris has maintained a steady review rhythm with the steering group, and decisions from the most recent review have been logged and circulated to this audience.
- **Vendor engagement:** The contract with Satisen Labs, worth $3.4M, is active, and working sessions continue with their delivery staff. The contract with Dilhas Consulting, worth $6.5M, is likewise active, and the advisory workstream is producing regular outputs that feed into pilot planning.
- **Evidence gathering:** We have begun consolidating pilot observations into a structured format so that results can be compared against the success criteria agreed at the start of the pilot.
- **Stakeholder alignment:** The finance lead and the operations lead have both been briefed and have raised no blocking objections at this stage.

## Risks

1. **Scope drift during pilot.** Participants occasionally request additions that fall outside the agreed pilot boundary. If accepted without review, these could blur the results and complicate the final assessment. Mitigation: all change requests go through Thokro Pobris for a decision.
2. **Vendor coordination.** Two significant contracts, one with Satisen Labs and one with Dilhas Consulting, create dependencies that must stay synchronized. A slip in one stream could affect the other. Mitigation: a standing coordination checkpoint between both vendors and the project team.
3. **Contract exposure.** With a combined commitment across the two contracts, the steering group should expect scrutiny from finance. Mitigation: keep spend reporting current and tie further commitments to pilot outcomes.
4. **Evidence quality.** Pilot feedback is uneven across participant groups, which may weaken the conclusions. Mitigation: targeted follow-up with under-represented groups.
5. **Communication leakage.** Because the pilot is not yet publicly announced internally, informal discussion could create premature expectations. Mitigation: continue restricted distribution of this report.

## Next Steps

- Complete the consolidation of pilot findings and compare them with the agreed success criteria.
- Hold a joint review with Satisen Labs and Dilhas Consulting to confirm dependencies and surface any delivery concerns early.
- Thokro Pobris will prepare a draft recommendation on the future of Project Siduris for steering group discussion.
- Refresh the risk register and confirm owners for each mitigation above.
- Agree with the finance lead on the format for ongoing spend reporting related to both contracts.
- Decide, with this group, when and how to widen communication about the pilot beyond the current audience.

## Requests of This Group

Please send any concerns about scope, vendor performance, or communication handling to Thokro Pobris before the next steering review so they can be addressed in the recommendation draft.

Periodic Status Report: Paskian Platform Group and Gaskergur Harbor Workstream

**Distribution:** Restricted. Intended for the program sponsors and workstream leads only. Please do not forward beyond this list.

## Summary

This report covers the current reporting period for the Gaskergur Harbor effort at Zastama Industries. The Gaskergur Harbor is developed by the Paskian Platform Group, a group of 16 people. Overall, the work is moving at a steady pace, and the group has kept its focus on closing out open audit items while continuing build activity. We are writing this version for a small audience so that we can be candid about concerns that would not belong in a company-wide update.

The main message is that delivery is on course, but a few dependencies and review items need attention from sponsors before they become blockers. Details follow in the sections below.

## Progress

**Delivery and engineering.** The Paskian Platform Group continued development of the Gaskergur Harbor through the period. Work centered on stabilizing core components, tightening interfaces between modules, and reducing the backlog of lower-priority defects. The group held its regular planning and review sessions, and decisions from those sessions were recorded and shared with workstream leads.

**Audit follow-up.** The audit finding assigned to the Paskian Platform Group is tracked under the identifier DJ-7108-L. The group has been working through the remediation steps, documenting evidence as it goes, and preparing material for the next review with the internal audit contacts. We have not changed the scope of the remediation, and we expect the evidence package to be reviewed in the ordinary course.

**Payments reconciliation.** Thokro Pobris works as a Solutions Architect and focuses on payments reconciliation. In this period, Thokro Pobris worked with engineering and the finance lead to clarify how reconciliation flows should behave at the edges of the platform, including how mismatches are surfaced and how exceptions are routed for human review. Thokro Pobris also contributed design notes that the wider group is using to align implementation choices. These notes reduced the number of open questions the engineers raised in review.

**Coordination.** Communication with adjacent teams has been consistent. Stakeholders from finance and operations have been briefed on the design direction, and their feedback has been incorporated where practical. A vendor-facing integration discussion also continued, with no change in position from either side.

## Risks

1. **Audit closure timing.** The remediation tied to the audit finding depends on reviewers being available to examine evidence. If review slots slip, closure could drift even though the technical work is complete. Mitigation: request reviewer availability early and keep the evidence package current.

2. **Reconciliation complexity.** Payments reconciliation has many edge cases, and some depend on decisions that sit outside the group, such as policy on how long unresolved exceptions may remain open. Without those decisions, engineers may build to assumptions that later need rework. Mitigation: ask the finance lead for a policy answer and record it in the design notes.

3. **Capacity concentration.** Specialized knowledge about reconciliation is concentrated in a small number of people. If one of them becomes unavailable, progress on that area could slow. Mitigation: encourage documentation and pairing so that knowledge spreads across the group.

4. **External dependency.** The vendor-facing integration discussion remains unresolved. Delays there could affect integration testing. Mitigation: set a clear decision point with the vendor and prepare a fallback approach for testing.

5. **Scope pressure.** Requests from adjacent teams continue to arrive. Taking on too many could dilute focus. Mitigation: route new requests through the existing planning session and weigh them against current commitments.

## Next Steps

Attendees discussed how to keep spending visible against the approved budget. The finance representative suggested a regular, lightweight reporting rhythm so that no team is surprised by cost movement. Krilfia Mukela, a Solutions Architect, said the technical design work should be documented clearly so that the services delivered under the contract can be checked against what was planned. She stressed that clear interface descriptions reduce rework, and rework is the most common source of avoidable cost on engagements like this.

The procurement representative added that anyone who needs to engage Misginine Systems should route requests through the project owner, rather than contacting the vendor directly. This avoids duplicate requests and keeps the contract scope clean.

**Project Nuzeor**

Next, the group discussed Project Nuzeor, which is targeting completion in Q3 FY26. The program management representative said the target remains the planning anchor and that dependencies should be raised early if any of them threaten it. No change to the target was proposed in this meeting. Attendees agreed that the main risk to any completion target is late discovery of dependencies, so teams were encouraged to flag blockers as soon as they appear instead of waiting for a scheduled review.

The representative of the Fonathe Platform Group reminded everyone that the Fonathe Platform Group is responsible for fleet telemetry. Identity and Access Tooling at Zastama Industries: Ownership, Budget, and Key Contacts

**Summary:** This page explains who owns identity and access tooling, how that work is funded, and where to direct common questions. It also notes a few related facts about the Fibrasine Relay and an external vendor agreement. All employees are welcome to use this page as a quick reference.

## Why this page exists

Questions about logging in, requesting permissions, and managing credentials come up constantly. Employees often are not sure whom to ask, and requests end up bouncing between groups. This page gives a single, plain-language description of who is responsible for identity and access tooling, so that questions reach the right people the first time.

It is intended for everyone at Zastama Industries, regardless of department or seniority. You do not need a technical background to use it.

## Who owns identity and access tooling

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is responsible for identity and access tooling. That covers the systems employees use to prove who they are and the systems that decide what each person is allowed to reach. If you have a question about how sign-in works, how access is granted, or how a tool connects to company identity systems, this is the group that owns the answer.

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is headed by Givien Mubren. Givien Mubren is also a member of the Gelgos Infrastructure Team, which means the person who leads the group works directly within it rather than sitting apart from it. Employees who need to escalate an issue, propose a change to how access works, or raise a concern about tooling direction can start with Givien Mubren.

For routine matters, such as a locked account or a missing permission, please use the standard internal request process first. Escalating directly is best reserved for issues that have stalled, that affect many people, or that involve a change in approach.

## Budget and resourcing

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team operates on an annual budget of $0.4M. That figure covers the group's work on identity and access tooling. It is a modest budget, and the team makes tradeoffs about what to improve first.

Because resources are limited, requests that come with a clear business reason, a description of who is affected, and a sense of urgency are much easier to prioritize. If you are planning a project that will depend on new access capabilities, talk to the team early, ideally before your own plans are finalized. Late requests are harder to fit in and may need to wait.

## Engineering leadership contact

Gonnom Gosmunza works as a Director of Engineering. Engineering managers and individual contributors who have questions about how identity and access work fits into broader engineering plans can raise them with Gonnom Gosmunza. This is a good route when a question spans several engineering groups rather than belonging to one tool or one request.

## Usage context: the Fibrasine Relay

The Fibrasine Relay has about 400 active users. When access changes are being planned, a user base of that size is worth keeping in mind, since changes to sign-in or permissions can reach a meaningful number of people at once. If your work touches the Fibrasine Relay, please let the owning group know about any planned access changes in advance so that users are not surprised.

## External vendor arrangement

Kremarel Partners holds a 24-month master services agreement. If your team works with Kremarel Partners and needs its staff to have access to internal systems, raise that early with the owners of identity and access tooling. Access for outside parties generally needs extra review, and the vendor relationship itself is managed separately from the day-to-day tooling. Please do not assume that the agreement alone grants access to anything.

## How to get help

1. Check the standard internal request process for routine access needs.
2. If the request has stalled or is unusual, contact the Gelgos Infrastructure Team.
3. For broader engineering questions, reach out to Gonnom Gosmunza.
4. For vendor access questions involving Kremarel Partners, notify the identity and access owners and your own manager before making assumptions.

## Keeping this page current

Ownership, budgets, and vendor arrangements change over time. If anything on this page looks out of date, please tell the page maintainer or edit it directly so the next reader has accurate information. A short, correct page is more useful to everyone than a long one that nobody trusts.

entities.description:

It is the broader entity referenced in the text, maintaining the page and benefiting from accurate information sharing. It is the organization where the Dankenor Analytics Unit, the Paskian Platform Group, and the Rishalen Integration Team are based. The company employs individuals such as the Director, Internal Controls and Vendor Governance, and the Fonathe Platform Group, and it is the context in which vendor contracts, audit findings, and escrow arrangements are reviewed.

It also organizes the Cross-Functional Sync meeting and publishes notes from such sessions to ensure consistent information across teams. The company manages procurement, facilities, security, and receiving teams for engagements such as Satisen Labs and Dilhas Consulting. Restricted Access Review: Vault Credential Records for Long-Tenured and Recent Staff

TO: Director of Security Operations
FROM: Manager, Access Governance
DATE: October 9, 2026
SUBJECT: Vault credential record review for two staff members

This memo is limited to the small group responsible for credential governance at Zastama Industries. Please do not forward it beyond that group. It summarizes the review of two vault credential records that surfaced during our routine access reconciliation, and it proposes how we handle similar cases going forward.

The first record concerns Thokro Pobris. Thokro Pobris joined the company in 2023, and the vault key ID assigned to Thokro Pobris is XX-6801-K. During reconciliation, we compared the key assignment against the onboarding records for that period and found the assignment consistent with the practices in place when the key was issued. We are not raising a discrepancy. We are including the record in this memo because it is the more recent of the two and therefore the better test of whether our current issuance process produces clean, traceable assignments.

The second record concerns Zosu Kistos. Zosu Kistos joined the company in 2020, which makes this employee one of the longer-tenured people in the review sample. Longer tenure matters for our purposes because credentials issued earlier were created under older procedures, which were less uniform about documenting who approved the issuance and when. We want to be careful not to read that as a finding of error. It is a reason to look more closely at how the paperwork was kept, and to confirm that nothing about the older records leaves a gap in our audit trail.

Comparing the two cases is useful precisely because they sit at different points in the company's history. The earlier record reflects an issuance process that relied heavily on informal approvals and manual notes. The later record reflects a process with more structure, though still not everything we would want. Seeing both side by side lets us judge which improvements have actually reduced ambiguity and which have only changed the format of the paperwork. We recommend treating the comparison as a process exercise rather than an evaluation of either individual, and we ask that nobody in this group draw conclusions about either employee from it.

We propose three next steps. First, the access governance team will confirm that each record has a named approver and a documented business reason on file, and will note any missing items without altering the underlying assignments. Second, we will ask the security engineering lead whether the older issuance records can be brought up to the same documentation standard as newer ones, and what effort that would involve. Third, we will draft a short checklist for future key issuance so that every assignment, regardless of when it is made, carries the same minimum evidence.

There are a few handling points. Key identifiers should not be copied into general-purpose channels, tickets visible to wider teams, or shared documents outside this group. If someone needs to verify a key, they should do so through the vault's own administrative interface rather than by circulating the identifier. If you believe a record has been shared more widely than intended, tell the access governance team promptly so we can assess whether any remediation is warranted.

Please send comments on the proposed steps to the access governance team by the end of next week. We will incorporate feedback and bring a consolidated recommendation to the next restricted review session. Until then, no changes to either assignment are planned, and routine access should continue as usual for both employees.

Thank you for your attention and discretion on this matter.

Onboarding Handoff and Budget Coding for Restricted Access Group

From: Operations Manager
To: Finance Lead; Program Coordinator
Subject: Handoff notes for the restricted access group

Hi both,

Before we widen this conversation, I want to keep it to the three of us. We need to settle how the handoff of recurring approvals will work for the restricted access group, and I'd rather not circulate the details company-wide yet.

For background, Zosu Kistos joined the company in 2020, so she has the longest history with how these approvals have been handled. Thokro Pobris joined the company in 2023 and will be picking up part of that workload. I'd like her institutional knowledge captured before any responsibilities move.

Can each of you tell me what you need from me to make this clean? Please keep replies within this thread.

Thanks,
Operations Manager

---

From: Finance Lead
To: Operations Manager; Program Coordinator
Subject: RE: Handoff notes for the restricted access group

Thanks for keeping this narrow. From the finance side, my main concern is that charges land in the right place during the transition. Zosu Kistos currently charges this work to budget code GW-2651-D, and I want that to stay unchanged until we have agreed in writing how costs will be split.

I'd also like Thokro Pobris to confirm which approvals she expects to handle first, so I can set up review steps on my end. If we skip that, we risk duplicate approvals or gaps that are hard to untangle at month end.

I can prepare a short summary of the review steps once I hear back. I'll keep it limited to this group as well.

Finance Lead

---

From: Program Coordinator
