Platform Operations Overview: Who Runs Fleet Telemetry, Data Retention, and Relay Hosting

TO: All Employees, Zastama Industries
FROM: Office of the Chief Operating Officer
DATE: October 9, 2026
SUBJECT: Where fleet telemetry, data retention tooling, and relay hosting live, and who to contact

Colleagues,

Over the past several months, we have received a steady stream of questions about which group owns which piece of our platform infrastructure, where those groups work, and whom to approach when something needs attention. This memo answers those questions in one place. It is not a reorganization announcement. Nothing described here is changing. The aim is to make the current arrangement easier to find and understand, especially for newer employees and for teams that depend on platform services but do not interact with them daily.

**Fleet telemetry and the group behind it**

The Fonathe Platform Group is responsible for fleet telemetry. That includes the pipelines, collection services, and supporting systems that gather operational signals from our deployed fleet and make them usable by the rest of the company. If you rely on telemetry for dashboards, analysis, planning, or customer-facing reporting, this is the group that keeps that data flowing and that you should engage when you have questions about its availability or scope.

The Fonathe Platform Group operates on an annual budget of $4.1M. That budget covers its ongoing work and the tooling it maintains on behalf of the wider organization. We mention the figure not to invite scrutiny of any particular line item but because several teams have asked how a function this central is funded. It is funded as a dedicated platform group with its own budget, rather than through charge-backs from individual business units. Requests that would materially change the group's workload should go through the normal planning process so that they can be weighed against existing commitments.

**Where the group works**

The Fonathe Platform Group works out of the Brerponen Annex. The Brerponen Annex is located in the coastal region. Employees who need to meet with the group in person should coordinate in advance, as with any shared site, and should check with facilities about visitor access before traveling. Most day-to-day collaboration with the group already happens remotely, and we expect that to continue. If you are planning a working session that would benefit from being in the same room, please raise it early so that the group can plan around its own delivery schedule.

**Data retention tooling**

Fallem Purraren focuses on data retention tooling. This work matters to everyone who produces or consumes data at Zastama Industries, because retention decisions affect storage costs, audit readiness, and our ability to answer questions about past operations. If your team has questions about how long particular categories of data are kept, how retention rules are applied, or how tooling might support a new requirement, Fallem Purraren is the right person to start with. The Feltarel Relay is scheduled to launch in Q4 FY26. Because the window is close, workspace and staffing decisions can no longer be treated as secondary to engineering milestones. For tracking purposes, the Feltarel Relay is administered under contract number SJ-7058-R, and any purchasing, staffing, or facilities request that depends on the program should reference that contract through the usual channels. Please do not circulate the contract number outside this group.

Development responsibility sits with the Paskian Platform Group, which continues to own the technical work leading up to launch. Our role in Program Operations is to make sure the surrounding conditions are ready, so that the engineering group is not slowed down by logistics. That includes space, access, and the coordination of people who will support the launch period, whether they are directly assigned or joining on a rotating basis.

The central planning constraint is physical capacity. The Renzer Field Office has capacity for 240 seats. That figure is a hard ceiling for planning purposes, and we should not assume it can be stretched through informal arrangements. Any proposal that would place launch-support staff at the Renzer Field Office needs to be tested against that number alongside the existing occupants, including permanent staff, visiting colleagues, and contractors. If the combined demand cannot be accommodated, we will need to consider staggered schedules, remote participation, or alternative arrangements, and I would prefer that we identify those options now rather than during the final weeks.

To move this forward, I am asking for the following. The Facilities Planning Lead should review current seat assignments at the Renzer Field Office and flag any seats that are reserved but rarely used, so we have an honest view of what is actually available. The Workforce Operations Lead should consolidate a draft list of roles expected to be on site during the launch period, without attaching names at this stage, and identify which roles could reasonably work remotely. Program leadership should confirm with the Paskian Platform Group which of its contributors need to be co-located and for how long, since that will drive most of the demand.

I recognize that some of these inputs depend on decisions that are not yet final. Where that is the case, please provide your best working assumption and state clearly that it is an assumption. Incomplete but candid information is more useful to me than polished figures that may change.

I would like each recipient to respond with their input in time for our next scheduled planning review. I will consolidate the responses into a single seating and staffing plan and circulate it to this same distribution only. If you believe someone should be added to the list, please raise it with me directly rather than forwarding this memo.

Thank you for your attention to this. Early, frank coordination now will make the launch period considerably smoother for everyone involved.

Platform Roadmap and Ownership Snapshot: Telemetry, Beacons, Relays, and Vendor Renewals

**Summary**

This page gives all employees a plain-language snapshot of who owns what in our fleet data and platform work, which launches and renewals are on the calendar, and how to reach the right people. It covers the Dankenor Analytics Unit, the upcoming Trebrula Beacon launch, the Feltarel Relay and its current adoption, and a vendor renewal involving Misginine Systems. Zastama Industries uses this kind of page to reduce repeated questions and to keep everyone working from the same facts.

**Who owns fleet telemetry**

The Dankenor Analytics Unit is responsible for fleet telemetry. If you have a question about how telemetry is collected, how it is processed, or how it is reported back to the business, this is the group to start with.

Two people on that group are worth knowing about. Krilfia Mukela is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Getaine Hebruen is also a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit, and Getaine Hebruen reports to Krilfia Mukela. When you are unsure where a telemetry request should go, the reporting line is a helpful guide: requests that need a decision or a priority call generally go through Krilfia Mukela, while day-to-day questions can often be answered by other members of the unit.

A few practical tips for working with the unit:

- Describe the business question first, then the data you think you need. The unit can often suggest a better route to the answer.
- Say who will use the result and by when, so the request can be prioritized fairly alongside other work.
- Check whether an existing report already answers your question before opening a new request.
- Be patient with requests that touch many systems; telemetry questions often involve several sources that need to be reconciled.

**Engineering leadership**

Gonnom Gosmunza works as a Director of Engineering. Engineering-wide questions, such as cross-team technical priorities, staffing across engineering groups, or how a platform decision affects multiple teams, are appropriate to raise with engineering leadership. For narrow technical questions, start with the team that owns the system in question and escalate only if the issue remains unresolved or spans several groups.

**Upcoming launch: the Trebrula Beacon**

The Trebrula Beacon is scheduled to launch in Q1 FY27. Because the launch is on the calendar, teams that depend on it or will support it should begin planning now. Useful preparation includes:

- Reviewing which of your processes will change when the launch happens.
- Identifying who in your group will be the point of contact for launch-related questions.
- Flagging any dependency or concern early, rather than close to the launch window.
- Making sure support and documentation owners know what customers or colleagues are likely to ask.

Launch timing is a plan, not a guarantee, and plans can move. Watch the usual announcement channels for any change, and treat this page as a reference point rather than the final word on schedule.

**Current offering: the Feltarel Relay**

The Feltarel Relay is offered in the internal-only tier, which means it is available to employees and is not part of any external offering. The Feltarel Relay has about 1,800 active users. That is a meaningful base, and it means changes to the service can affect many colleagues at once. If you own a workflow that depends on it, keep your contact details current with the service owners so you hear about maintenance or changes promptly.

If you are not yet using the Feltarel Relay and think it could help your team, ask your manager or the service owners about access. Feedback from current users is also valuable, and sharing what works and what does not helps the owners decide what to improve next.

**Vendor renewal: Misginine Systems**

Misginine Systems is up for renewal in Q4 FY28. Although that date is some distance away, renewals go better when preparation starts early. Teams that rely on the vendor should consider the following:

- Collect honest feedback on how well the service has met your needs.
- Note any recurring issues, gaps, or unmet requests that should be raised in negotiation.
- Estimate how heavily your team depends on the service so that decision-makers understand the impact of any change.
- Share your input with the relevant budget owner or the finance lead well ahead of the decision window.

Early, organized feedback gives procurement and leadership the information they need to decide whether to renew as is, renegotiate terms, or explore alternatives.

**Where to go with questions**

- Telemetry and analytics: begin with the Dankenor Analytics Unit.
- Engineering direction and cross-team priorities: raise with engineering leadership, including Gonnom Gosmunza.
- Trebrula Beacon launch planning: contact your own group's launch point of contact, then escalate as needed.
- Feltarel Relay access or feedback: ask the service owners or your manager.
- Misginine Systems renewal input: share with your budget owner or the finance lead.

This page will be updated as plans change. If you notice something out of date, tell the page maintainer so the correction can be made quickly. Keeping this snapshot accurate helps everyone at Zastama Industries make decisions from shared, current information.

The **Paskian Platform Group** is a team within **Zastama Industries** responsible for the technical development and management of the **Gaskergur Harbor** project. The group consists of 16 members and is led by **Pethisa Hebroren**, who focuses on **data retention tooling** and leads the effort for the group [1].

### Key Responsibilities and Activities

1. **Gaskergur Harbor Development**:
   - The Paskian Platform Group is responsible for the development and stabilization of the **Gaskergur Harbor**, a project with approximately 6,300 active users. The group focuses on stabilizing core components, reducing the **defect backlog**, and addressing **audit findings** [1].
   - The group is working on **remediation steps** for the audit finding **DJ-7108-L**, preparing evidence for the next internal audit review [1].

2. **Data Retention Tooling**:
   - The group is developing **data retention tooling** to manage how long data is retained, archived, or deleted. This includes refining **retention rules**, improving **audit logging**, and addressing **edge cases** in datasets with mixed retention requirements [2].
   - The group is also working with **Thikama Harlurine**, a data scientist, to analyze how data is used and aged across datasets, which informs the definition of **retention categories** [2].

3. **Payments Reconciliation**:
   - **Thokro Pobris**, a **Solutions Architect** within the group, focuses on **payments reconciliation**. The group has been working with the **finance lead** to clarify how mismatches are surfaced and how exceptions are routed for human review [1].

4. **Coordination and Communication**:
   - The group maintains consistent communication with **adjacent teams**, including **finance** and **operations**, to ensure alignment on design directions and feedback incorporation [1].
   - The group also engages in **vendor-facing integration discussions**, although these remain unresolved [1].

### Risks and Challenges

1. **Audit Closure Timing**:
   - The **remediation** of the audit finding **DJ-7108-L** depends on the availability of reviewers. If review slots slip, the closure could be delayed despite the technical work being complete [1].

2. **Reconciliation Complexity**:
   - **Payments reconciliation** involves many **edge cases**, and some depend on decisions from outside the group. Without clear policy answers, engineers may build to assumptions that later require rework [1].

3. **Capacity Concentration**:
   - Specialized knowledge about **reconciliation** is concentrated in a small number of people. If one of them becomes unavailable, progress could slow [1].

4. **External Dependency**:
   - The **vendor-facing integration** discussion remains unresolved, and delays could affect **integration testing** [1].

5. **Scope Pressure**:
   - Requests from **adjacent teams** continue to arrive, and taking on too many could dilute the group's focus [1].

### Next Steps

1. The group will continue **remediation work** and prepare the **evidence package** for the next **audit review** [1].
2. **Thokro Pobris** will finalize **reconciliation design notes** and review them with the **finance lead** to confirm policy assumptions before more implementation begins [1].
3. The group will keep reducing the **defect backlog** and report on **stability** at the next review [1].
4. **Workstream leads** will confirm **reviewer availability** for **audit sessions** [1].
5. Sponsors are asked to help secure a decision on the **outstanding vendor integration question** and to weigh in on any **scope requests** that conflict with current priorities [1].

### Leadership and Reporting

- The **Paskian Platform Group** is part of **Zastama Industries**, and its work is overseen by the **Business Lead**, who provides authoritative information regarding **ownership details** and **launch timing** [1].
- The group is also responsible for the **technical development** of the **Feltarel Relay**, and **logistics** are being coordinated to ensure the group is not slowed down during the **development and launch** of the **Feltarel Relay** [1].

### Budget and Funding

- The **budget code** for **Pethisa Hebroren** is **SP-9062-V**, and all related costs are reported against this code [2].
- The **finance lead** has not raised any **reconciliation issues** this period [2].

### Conclusion

The **Paskian Platform Group** plays a critical role in the development and management of the **Gaskergur Harbor** and **data retention tooling** at **Zastama Industries**. The group is focused on stabilizing core components, addressing **audit findings**, and ensuring **payments reconciliation** is handled effectively. Despite facing several **risks and challenges**, the group is working to maintain **delivery on course** and is preparing for the next **audit review** and **vendor integration decisions** [1].

Periodic Status Report: Paskian Platform Group and Gaskergur Harbor Workstream

**Distribution:** Restricted. Intended for the program sponsors and workstream leads only. Please do not forward beyond this list.

## Summary

This report covers the current reporting period for the Gaskergur Harbor effort at Zastama Industries. The Gaskergur Harbor is developed by the Paskian Platform Group, a group of 16 people. Overall, the work is moving at a steady pace, and the group has kept its focus on closing out open audit items while continuing build activity. We are writing this version for a small audience so that we can be candid about concerns that would not belong in a company-wide update.

The main message is that delivery is on course, but a few dependencies and review items need attention from sponsors before they become blockers. Details follow in the sections below.

## Progress

**Delivery and engineering.** The Paskian Platform Group continued development of the Gaskergur Harbor through the period. Work centered on stabilizing core components, tightening interfaces between modules, and reducing the backlog of lower-priority defects. The group held its regular planning and review sessions, and decisions from those sessions were recorded and shared with workstream leads.

**Audit follow-up.** The audit finding assigned to the Paskian Platform Group is tracked under the identifier DJ-7108-L. The group has been working through the remediation steps, documenting evidence as it goes, and preparing material for the next review with the internal audit contacts. We have not changed the scope of the remediation, and we expect the evidence package to be reviewed in the ordinary course.

**Payments reconciliation.** Thokro Pobris works as a Solutions Architect and focuses on payments reconciliation. In this period, Thokro Pobris worked with engineering and the finance lead to clarify how reconciliation flows should behave at the edges of the platform, including how mismatches are surfaced and how exceptions are routed for human review. Thokro Pobris also contributed design notes that the wider group is using to align implementation choices. These notes reduced the number of open questions the engineers raised in review.

**Coordination.** Communication with adjacent teams has been consistent. Stakeholders from finance and operations have been briefed on the design direction, and their feedback has been incorporated where practical. A vendor-facing integration discussion also continued, with no change in position from either side.

## Risks

1. **Audit closure timing.** The remediation tied to the audit finding depends on reviewers being available to examine evidence. If review slots slip, closure could drift even though the technical work is complete. Mitigation: request reviewer availability early and keep the evidence package current.

2. **Reconciliation complexity.** Payments reconciliation has many edge cases, and some depend on decisions that sit outside the group, such as policy on how long unresolved exceptions may remain open. Without those decisions, engineers may build to assumptions that later need rework. Mitigation: ask the finance lead for a policy answer and record it in the design notes.

3. **Capacity concentration.** Specialized knowledge about reconciliation is concentrated in a small number of people. If one of them becomes unavailable, progress on that area could slow. Mitigation: encourage documentation and pairing so that knowledge spreads across the group.

4. **External dependency.** The vendor-facing integration discussion remains unresolved. Delays there could affect integration testing. Mitigation: set a clear decision point with the vendor and prepare a fallback approach for testing.

5. **Scope pressure.** Requests from adjacent teams continue to arrive. Taking on too many could dilute focus. Mitigation: route new requests through the existing planning session and weigh them against current commitments.

## Next Steps

- The Paskian Platform Group will continue remediation work and prepare the evidence package for the next audit review.
- Thokro Pobris will finalize the reconciliation design notes and review them with the finance lead so that policy assumptions are confirmed before more implementation begins.
- Engineering will keep reducing the defect backlog and will report on stability at the next review.
- Workstream leads will confirm reviewer availability for audit sessions.
- Sponsors are asked to help secure a decision on the outstanding vendor integration question and to weigh in on any scope requests that conflict with current priorities.
- The next status report will update the items above and note any changes in risk levels.

## Closing Note

Please send questions or corrections to the report owner directly. Because this report is restricted, we ask that comments stay within the distribution list until the risks above are better understood.

Data Retention Tooling Status Report for the Paskian Platform Group

**Distribution: Restricted. Please do not forward beyond the named recipients.**

## Summary

This report covers the current state of data retention tooling work at Zastama Industries. The Paskian Platform Group is headed by Pethisa Hebroren, who focuses on data retention tooling. Overall, the effort is moving steadily. The core design questions have been narrowed, and the remaining work is mostly about validation, documentation, and agreeing on rollout sequencing with the teams that will depend on the tooling. Because this report goes to a small audience, it includes candid notes on open concerns that we would not yet put in a broader update.

## Progress

**Ownership and funding.** Spending for the work is tracked under a single budget line. The budget code for Pethisa Hebroren is SP-9062-V, and all related costs continue to be reported against it. The finance lead has not raised any reconciliation issues this period.

**Tooling work.** The group has continued refining how retention rules are defined, applied, and audited. Work this period centered on making policy definitions easier to review, tightening the way deletion and archival actions are logged, and clarifying which datasets fall under which rules. Early internal testing has surfaced several edge cases around datasets with mixed retention requirements, and these are being triaged.

Zastama Industries Periodic Status Report: Engineering, Analytics, and Product Access Update

## Summary

This report gives all employees a plain-language view of where cross-functional work stands this period. Overall, work is progressing steadily. Teams are meeting their planned milestones, collaboration between engineering and analytics is improving, and the main open items concern access controls and how we communicate product availability. Nothing in this report requires action from most employees, but we encourage everyone to read the Risks and Next Steps sections, since some of those items may affect how you request tools and data.

We want to use this report to help colleagues understand who is working on what.

Gonnom Gosmunza joined the company in 2023 and works as a Director of Engineering. Gonnom Gosmunza is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on identity and access tooling. That focus matters to nearly everyone, because identity and access tooling determines how employees sign in, how permissions are granted, and how quickly access can be reviewed or removed. Zosu Kistos is also a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. The unit's work blends data analysis with engineering practice, and having both colleagues in the same group has helped shorten the loop between identifying a data need and building the tooling that supports it.

On reporting lines, Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. We mention this because several recent cross-team requests were routed unclearly, and knowing the reporting structure helps requests reach the right decision-maker the first time. If your work touches either of them, please direct approvals and escalations through the established reporting line rather than around it.

## Progress

**Identity and access tooling.** Work continued on simplifying how permissions are requested and reviewed. The focus this period was reducing manual steps, making approval paths easier to follow, and improving the audit trail so reviewers can see who has access to what and why. Early internal feedback has been positive, particularly about clearer request forms.

**Analytics collaboration.** The Dankenor Analytics Unit continued to refine how shared datasets are documented and accessed. Documentation has become more consistent, and fewer ad hoc questions are reaching individual analysts because common answers are now easier to find.

5. **Adoption.** New tooling only helps if people use it. Without consistent adoption, the benefits to security and efficiency will be limited.

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is responsible for identity and access tooling. The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is headed by Givien Mubren. Givien Mubren is also a member of the Gelgos Infrastructure Team, which means the person who leads the group works directly within it rather than sitting apart from it. Employees who need to escalate an issue, propose a change to how access works, or raise a concern about tooling direction can start with Givien Mubren.

For routine matters, such as a locked account or a missing permission, please use the standard internal request process first. Escalating directly is best reserved for issues that have stalled, that affect many people, or that involve a change in approach.

The Gelgos Infrastructure Team operates on an annual budget of $0.4M. That figure covers the group's work on identity and access tooling. It is a modest budget, and the team makes tradeoffs about what to improve first.

Because resources are limited, requests that come with a clear business reason, a description of who is affected, and a sense of urgency are much easier to prioritize. If you are planning a project that will depend on new access capabilities, talk to the team early, ideally before your own plans are finalized. Late requests are harder to fit in and may need to wait.

Gonnom Gosmunza works as a Director of Engineering. Engineering managers and individual contributors who have questions about how identity and access work fits into broader engineering plans can raise them with Gonnom Gosmunza. The Fibrasine Relay has about 400 active users. Kremarel Partners holds a 24-month master services agreement. entities.name: Dankenor Analytics Unit
entities.description:
The Dankenor Analytics Unit is a department within Zastama Industries responsible for a wide range of analytics-related functions across the company. It operates on an annual budget of $6.4M and is composed of 38 members who provide data-driven insights to support forecasting, decision-making, and business strategy. The unit blends data analysis with engineering practice, working on identity and access tooling, shared dataset documentation, and the development of internal analytics infrastructure.

One of its key responsibilities is fleet telemetry, where it collects, processes, and reports telemetry data back to the business, serving as the primary point of contact for all telemetry-related inquiries and requests. Additionally, the unit is tasked with analyzing how heavily each vendor's services are used, offering insights that inform resource allocation and vendor management strategies.

The Dankenor Analytics Unit also plays a central role in governance and project sponsorship, particularly for initiatives such as Project Stebril, which it owns and oversees. It provides governance, prioritization, and escalation paths for the project. The unit supports teams across the company with analysis and reporting, and is the right place to begin for questions about reports, data analysis, and decision-informing data. It is led by members such as Pivoine Geltoett and is recognized as a critical internal resource for both quantitative and qualitative research and analytics work.<SEP>A unit at Zastama Industries responsible for handling analytics-related requests.

entities.name: Vadesis Gummenbel
entities.description:
Vadesis Gummenbel is a Chief of Staff at Zastama Industries and a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. In their role, they support cross-functional coordination, communication, and decision recording across the company. Vadesis facilitates meetings, ensures communication clarity, and helps coordinate priorities among different groups. They are also responsible for circulating notes to all employees and scheduling cross-functional updates.

As a key contact for unclear requests or workstreams, Vadesis Gummenbel serves as a first point of contact for issues that lack clear ownership. They have sent company-wide clarifications on analytics funding and project ownership and have responded to follow-up inquiries from a Finance Lead. Additionally, they provide feedback on the feasibility of data retention approaches for Project Soramis and have commented on seating arrangements for Project Nolaor.

Beyond their internal coordination duties, Vadesis is one of the contacts for questions related to the usage data of vendors' services, further highlighting their role in bridging operational and analytical functions within the organization.<SEP>Vadesis Gummenbel is a person who reports to Zosne Bramfa and is involved in the day-to-day delivery of the Gaskergur Harbor engagement.<SEP>An individual responsible for data retention tooling and reporting to Zosne Bramfa. The escrow reference for Vadesis Gummenbel is WX-1844-U.

entities.name: Lagemett Ledger
entities.description:
The Lagemett Ledger is a system or document used by Zastama Industries to track components and dependencies related to a project. It serves as a foundational system for both Project Stebril and Project Rakresett, ensuring consistency, avoiding duplicated effort, and maintaining clarity in data and record changes. Changes to the Lagemett Ledger can impact Project Rakresett, and its stakeholders are advised to be involved in discussions regarding such modifications.

The system is an internal-only product, primarily used by Zastama Industries employees, with approximately 2,600 active users. It is scheduled to launch in Q3 FY27 and is part of the company’s internal platform roadmap. The Lagemett Ledger relies on components supplied by multiple external vendors, including Misginine Systems and Dilhas Consulting, each responsible for different parts of the build. Additionally, it is noted that the system or component uses parts supplied by Nalzenett Labs.

The Lagemett Ledger is also described as an artifact associated with vendor arrangements and is mentioned in the context of potential process updates from procurement. Its role in vendor management and internal coordination is emphasized, with discussions around interface ownership and platform development being part of ongoing internal meetings.

Periodic Status Report: Paskian Platform Group and Gaskergur Harbor Workstream

**Distribution:** Restricted. Intended for the program sponsors and workstream leads only. Please do not forward beyond this list.

## Summary

This report covers the current reporting period for the Gaskergur Harbor effort at Zastama Industries. The Gaskergur Harbor is developed by the Paskian Platform Group, a group of 16 people. Overall, the work is moving at a steady pace, and the group has kept its focus on closing out open audit items while continuing build activity. We are writing this version for a small audience so that we can be candid about concerns that would not belong in a company-wide update.

The main message is that delivery is on course, but a few dependencies and review items need attention from sponsors before they become blockers. Details follow in the sections below.

## Progress

**Delivery and engineering.** The Paskian Platform Group continued development of the Gaskergur Harbor through the period. Work centered on stabilizing core components, tightening interfaces between modules, and reducing the backlog of lower-priority defects. The group held its regular planning and review sessions, and decisions from those sessions were recorded and shared with workstream leads.

**Audit follow-up.** The audit finding assigned to the Paskian Platform Group is tracked under the identifier DJ-7108-L. The group has been working through the remediation steps, documenting evidence as it goes, and preparing material for the next review with the internal audit contacts. We have not changed the scope of the remediation, and we expect the evidence package to be reviewed in the ordinary course.

**Payments reconciliation.** Thokro Pobris works as a Solutions Architect and focuses on payments reconciliation. In this period, Thokro Pobris worked with engineering and the finance lead to clarify how reconciliation flows should behave at the edges of the platform, including how mismatches are surfaced and how exceptions are routed for human review. Thokro Pobris also contributed design notes that the wider group is using to align implementation choices. These notes reduced the number of open questions the engineers raised in review.

**Coordination.** Communication with adjacent teams has been consistent. Stakeholders from finance and operations have been briefed on the design direction, and their feedback has been incorporated where practical. A vendor-facing integration discussion also continued, with no change in position from either side.

## Risks

1. **Audit closure timing.** The remediation tied to the audit finding depends on reviewers being available to examine evidence. If review slots slip, closure could drift even though the technical work is complete. Mitigation: request reviewer availability early and keep the evidence package current.

2. **Reconciliation complexity.** Payments reconciliation has many edge cases, and some depend on decisions that sit outside the group, such as policy on how long unresolved exceptions may remain open. Without those decisions, engineers may build to assumptions that later need rework. Mitigation: ask the finance lead for a policy answer and record it in the design notes.

3. **Capacity concentration.** Specialized knowledge about reconciliation is concentrated in a small number of people. If one of them becomes unavailable, progress on that area could slow. Mitigation: encourage documentation and pairing so that knowledge spreads across the group.

4. **External dependency.** The vendor-facing integration discussion remains unresolved. Delays there could affect integration testing. Mitigation: set a clear decision point with the vendor and prepare a fallback approach for testing.

5. **Scope pressure.** Requests from adjacent teams continue to arrive. Taking on too many could dilute focus. Mitigation: route new requests through the existing planning session and weigh them against current commitments.

## Next Steps

- The Paskian Platform Group will continue remediation work and prepare the evidence package for the next audit review.
- Thokro Pobris will finalize the reconciliation design notes and review them with the finance lead so that policy assumptions are confirmed before more implementation begins.
- Engineering will keep reducing the defect backlog and will report on stability at the next review.
- Workstream leads will confirm reviewer availability for audit sessions.
- Sponsors are asked to help secure a decision on the outstanding vendor integration question and to weigh in on any scope requests that conflict with current priorities.
- The next status report will update the items above and note any changes in risk levels.

## Closing Note

Please send questions or corrections to the report owner directly. Because this report is restricted, we ask that comments stay within the distribution list until the risks above are better understood.

Data Retention Tooling Status Report for the Paskian Platform Group

**Distribution: Restricted. Please do not forward beyond the named recipients.**

## Summary

This report covers the current state of data retention tooling work at Zastama Industries. The Paskian Platform Group is headed by Pethisa Hebroren, who focuses on data retention tooling. Overall, the effort is moving steadily. The core design questions have been narrowed, and the remaining work is mostly about validation, documentation, and agreeing on rollout sequencing with the teams that will depend on the tooling. Because this report goes to a small audience, it includes candid notes on open concerns that we would not yet put in a broader update.

## Progress

**Ownership and funding.** Spending for the work is tracked under a single budget line. The budget code for Pethisa Hebroren is SP-9062-V, and all related costs continue to be reported against it. The finance lead has not raised any reconciliation issues this period.

**Tooling work.** The group has continued refining how retention rules are defined, applied, and audited. Work this period centered on making policy definitions easier to review, tightening the way deletion and archival actions are logged, and clarifying which datasets fall under which rules. Early internal testing has surfaced several edge cases around datasets with mixed retention requirements, and these are being triaged.

**Analytical support.** Thikama Harlurine, a Data Scientist who joined the company in 2023, has been supporting the effort by examining how data is actually used and aged across the datasets in scope. Her analysis is informing which retention categories are practical and where the current definitions are too coarse. Her findings have been shared with the group in working sessions and are feeding directly into the next revision of the rule definitions.

**Coordination.** Discussions with legal and compliance contacts have continued. The main outcome is a shared understanding of the review process for any retention rule that changes how long sensitive records are kept. A security reviewer has also asked to see the audit logging approach before it is finalized.

## Risks

1. **Ambiguous requirements.** Some retention obligations are interpreted differently by different stakeholders. If these are not resolved soon, rules may need to be reworked after testing, which would cost time.
2. **Dataset complexity.** Datasets with mixed requirements may need to be split or tagged more granularly. This could expand scope if the number of affected datasets is larger than expected.
3. **Dependency timing.** Downstream teams have their own priorities, and their availability for integration testing is uncertain. Delays there could push back the rollout sequence.
4. **Irreversible actions.** Deletion is inherently hard to undo. Until safeguards and review steps are fully validated, we are keeping the tooling in a conservative, non-destructive mode for anything beyond test data.
5. **Capacity.** Analytical and engineering effort is concentrated among a few people. Absence or competing requests could slow progress.

## Next Steps

- Resolve the open interpretation questions with legal and compliance, and record the decisions in writing.
- Incorporate the latest usage analysis from Thikama Harlurine into a revised set of retention categories.
- Complete the review of audit logging with the security reviewer and address any feedback.
- Triage and close out the edge cases found in early testing, prioritizing those involving mixed retention requirements.
- Agree on a rollout sequence with downstream teams, including a clear checkpoint before any destructive action is enabled outside of test data.
- Prepare a short follow-up for the next reporting period, covering decisions made, remaining risks, and any change in resourcing needs.

## Closing Note

Pethisa Hebroren and the Paskian Platform Group will flag any item that threatens the planned sequence as soon as it is identified, rather than waiting for the next scheduled report. Questions about this report can be directed to the group directly. Please keep the contents within the restricted audience, as several items remain under discussion and are subject to change.

Identity Tooling and Budget Status Report, Restricted Distribution

**Distribution note:** This report is intended for a small group of leads and sponsors at Zastama Industries. Please do not forward it beyond the approved list, as it touches on access infrastructure details.

## Summary

This period's report covers two areas of interest to the restricted group: the state of identity and access tooling, and the financial footing of Project Pirpoan. Overall, work is proceeding in line with expectations, and no matters currently require escalation to executive sponsors. The sections below describe progress, open risks, and the actions planned for the coming cycle.

The Rishalen Integration Team is responsible for identity and access tooling, and its work underpins several of the dependencies that other efforts rely on. Project Pirpoan has an approved budget of $5.5M, and that figure remains the reference point for all planning discussions summarized here.

## Progress

Identity and access tooling continues to be handled by the Rishalen Integration Team, which has kept its work organized around controlled credential handling. For traceability, the vault key ID for the Rishalen Integration Team is RH-4278-L. Access to that key remains limited to the people who need it, and the group has continued its practice of reviewing who holds access whenever responsibilities change.

On the financial side, the approved budget for Project Pirpoan has been held steady, and no change request has been raised against it. The finance lead has confirmed that tracking against the approved amount continues to follow the normal review rhythm. Conversations between project stakeholders have focused on keeping scope aligned with that approved amount rather than expanding it.

Several supporting activities also moved forward:

- Review of how access requests are routed and approved was discussed with the relevant stakeholders.
- Documentation of operational procedures for credential handling was refreshed.
- Coordination meetings between the engineering leads and the finance lead were held to keep expectations consistent.

## Risks

**Dependency concentration.** Because the Rishalen Integration Team owns identity and access tooling, other efforts depend on its availability. If its capacity is stretched, downstream work could be delayed. This is being watched, though it is not yet an active problem.

**Credential handling.** Any identifier tied to a vault must be treated carefully. The main exposure is accidental circulation of this report or its contents. Recipients should keep it within the restricted audience and avoid copying details into broader channels.

**Budget discipline.** While Project Pirpoan remains within its approved budget of $5.5M, unplanned requests could create pressure on scope. Any such request should go through the normal change process and be reviewed by the finance lead before commitments are made.

**Vendor and procurement uncertainty.** Some external vendor decisions remain open in general terms. These could influence timing if they are not settled in a reasonable window.

## Next Steps

1. Continue the periodic review of who has access to the vault key and confirm that the list remains minimal.
2. Hold a short check-in between the Rishalen Integration Team and the engineering leads to assess capacity against upcoming dependencies.
3. Maintain monthly alignment between project stakeholders and the finance lead so that Project Pirpoan stays consistent with its approved budget.
4. Review the open vendor questions and agree on owners for closing them out.
5. Prepare the next periodic report for this same restricted group, highlighting any change in risk posture.

## Closing Note

If any recipient identifies a concern about distribution or access, please raise it directly with the report owner. Questions about financial tracking should go to the finance lead, and questions about identity tooling should go to the Rishalen Integration Team through its established channel.

Rishalen Integration Team: Access Handling and Working Notes

**Summary**

This page is for the small group of people working on the integration effort and for the few reviewers who support them. It is not intended for company-wide circulation at Zastama Industries, so please do not forward it or paste its contents into broader channels. It records who is on the team, how credential references are handled, and what the next working steps look like.

**Team Membership**

Bedras Sarkua is a member of the Rishalen Integration Team. Milsean Trusases is also a member of the Rishalen Integration Team. Between them, they cover the day-to-day coordination of the integration work, including reviewing changes, confirming access needs, and keeping the working notes current. If you need something from the group, route the request through the team's normal intake rather than contacting individual members informally, so that requests are not lost.

**Credential References**

The team uses a vault to hold secrets needed for the integration. Only the reference identifier for a key should ever be written in documentation; the secret material itself must never appear on a wiki page, in a chat message, or in a ticket. For record-keeping purposes, Bedras Sarkua's vault key ID is XM-1748-X. This identifier is a pointer only and does not grant access on its own. Anyone who needs access must request it through the standard approval path, and the request should state the business reason and the expected duration.

If you believe a key reference has been exposed to someone who should not have it, tell the security contact right away. Do not wait for the next team meeting. Rotation is handled by the vault administrators, and the team should expect to be asked to confirm which systems depend on the affected key.

**Working Practices**

- Keep discussion of integration details within the restricted channel set up for this effort.
- Record decisions in this wiki rather than relying on chat history, which is hard to search later.
- When a change touches an external vendor, note it generically and involve the procurement lead before any commitments are made.
- Review access lists regularly and remove anyone who no longer has a need.
- Treat draft diagrams and test data as internal-only, even when they look harmless.

**Open Items and Next Steps**

Several items remain open and will be tracked here as they are resolved:

1. Confirm that all dependent systems reference the vault entry by identifier rather than by embedded secret.
2. Agree on a review cadence for access approvals with the security contact.
3. Document the escalation path for integration incidents, including who is on call and how handoffs are recorded.
4. Ask the finance lead whether any pending integration costs need to be flagged ahead of the next planning cycle.

**Maintenance of This Page**

Members of the Rishalen Integration Team own this page and should update it whenever membership, access practices, or open items change. Reviewers who notice an inaccuracy should leave a comment for the team rather than editing directly. If this page is ever moved to a wider audience, the credential section should be reviewed and, where appropriate, removed first. Questions about the page's scope or distribution can go to the documentation owner, who will confirm whether a wider audience is appropriate before anything is shared further.

Platform Operations Overview: Who Runs Fleet Telemetry, Data Retention, and Relay Hosting

TO: All Employees, Zastama Industries
FROM: Office of the Chief Operating Officer
DATE: October 9, 2026
SUBJECT: Where fleet telemetry, data retention tooling, and relay hosting live, and who to contact

Colleagues,

Over the past several months, we have received a steady stream of questions about which group owns which piece of our platform infrastructure, where those groups work, and whom to approach when something needs attention. This memo answers those questions in one place. It is not a reorganization announcement. Nothing described here is changing. The aim is to make the current arrangement easier to find and understand, especially for newer employees and for teams that depend on platform services but do not interact with them daily.

**Fleet telemetry and the group behind it**

The Fonathe Platform Group is responsible for fleet telemetry. That includes the pipelines, collection services, and supporting systems that gather operational signals from our deployed fleet and make them usable by the rest of the company. If you rely on telemetry for dashboards, analysis, planning, or customer-facing reporting, this is the group that keeps that data flowing and that you should engage when you have questions about its availability or scope.

The Fonathe Platform Group operates on an annual budget of $4.1M. That budget covers its ongoing work and the tooling it maintains on behalf of the wider organization. We mention the figure not to invite scrutiny of any particular line item but because several teams have asked how a function this central is funded. It is funded as a dedicated platform group with its own budget, rather than through charge-backs from individual business units. Requests that would materially change the group's workload should go through the normal planning process so that they can be weighed against existing commitments.

**Where the group works**

The Fonathe Platform Group works out of the Brerponen Annex. The Brerponen Annex is located in the coastal region. Employees who need to meet with the group in person should coordinate in advance, as with any shared site, and should check with facilities about visitor access before traveling. Most day-to-day collaboration with the group already happens remotely, and we expect that to continue. If you are planning a working session that would benefit from being in the same room, please raise it early so that the group can plan around its own delivery schedule.

**Data retention tooling**

Fallem Purraren focuses on data retention tooling. This work matters to everyone who produces or consumes data at Zastama Industries, because retention decisions affect storage costs, audit readiness, and our ability to answer questions about past operations. If your team has questions about how long particular categories of data are kept, how retention rules are applied, or how tooling might support a new requirement, Fallem Purraren is the right person to start with. Please bring a clear description of the data involved and the reason for your request, since this lets her give you a useful answer more quickly. Requests that touch legal or compliance obligations should also involve the relevant compliance contact, so that tooling decisions and policy decisions stay aligned.

**Relay hosting**

The Fibrasine Relay is hosted at the Kimmoine Annex. Teams that depend on the relay, whether directly or through a downstream service, should be aware that its physical hosting is separate from the location where the telemetry group works. This distinction is worth keeping in mind when you are diagnosing an issue or planning maintenance. A problem that appears to involve both telemetry and relay behavior may in fact involve two different sites, and the right first step is often to confirm which side of that boundary the symptoms point to. When you open a request, please say whether it concerns the relay, the telemetry pipelines, or both, so that it reaches the right people the first time.

**Reporting lines**

Zosu Kistos reports to Leroror Lukaine. We are including this because a number of employees have asked whom to escalate to when a matter cannot be resolved at the working level. In those cases, the escalation path runs through Leroror Lukaine. Please use that path thoughtfully. Most questions are best handled first with the person closest to the work, and escalation is most effective when you can summarize what has been tried, what is blocked, and what decision you need.

**How to get help efficiently**

To make the most of the people described above, we ask that everyone follow a few simple practices. First, identify which area your question belongs to: telemetry, data retention, or relay hosting. Second, write down the specific outcome you need, not only the symptom you are seeing. Third, include enough context that someone unfamiliar with your project can understand the request without a meeting. Fourth, respect that each of these groups has planned work, and that urgent requests should be reserved for genuine urgency.

We also encourage managers to share this memo with their teams and to point new hires to it during onboarding. If you notice that anything here is out of date or unclear, tell your manager or the operations office so that we can correct it. Clear ownership is one of the simplest ways we can reduce friction across the company, and we are grateful for the patience and professionalism with which teams have been working through these questions.

Thank you for your attention, and for the care you bring to the systems that so many of us rely on.

Office of the Chief Operating Officer

Restricted Access Working Notes: Budget Attribution and Architecture Review Coordination

**Summary**

This page is a working reference for the small group involved in the current architecture review and its associated budget tracking at Zastama Industries. It records who holds which responsibilities, how budget attribution is handled, and what the group expects to do next. It is not intended for company-wide circulation, so please do not forward it, paste excerpts into broader channels, or link it from open pages without checking with the page owner first.

**Purpose and Scope**

The group was formed to keep technical decisions and spending records aligned. In past cycles, design choices were sometimes made without a clear link to the budget line that would fund them, and finance later had to reconstruct the reasoning. This page exists to prevent that. It covers two things: the people and codes the group relies on day to day, and the working conventions we follow when a design decision has cost implications.

The page deliberately stays narrow. It does not describe vendor selection, customer commitments, or staffing plans. Those are handled elsewhere and are discussed only with the people who need to know.

**Key People and Budget Attribution**

Dankenor Analytics Unit: Who We Are and How to Work With Us

## Summary

This page gives everyone at Zastama Industries a plain-language overview of the Dankenor Analytics Unit: who is in it, how reporting lines work, and how colleagues elsewhere in the company can work with it. The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people. It brings together architecture, planning, and modeling skills so that business questions can be answered with evidence rather than guesswork.

Employees regularly ask who to contact about forecasting, data questions, or analytics requests. Until now the answers lived in scattered chat threads and personal notes. This page collects the essentials in one place so that new joiners and long-serving staff alike can find the right person quickly. It is meant as an orientation guide, not an org chart of record. If something here looks out of date, tell the page owner so it can be corrected.

## Unit overview

The Dankenor Analytics Unit has 38 people, and its members come from a mix of technical and operational backgrounds. Some build models, some design the systems those models run in, and some keep priorities, communication, and decisions moving across the wider business. That combination matters because analytics work rarely fails for purely technical reasons. More often it stalls because nobody agreed on the question, the owner was unclear, or the results never reached the people who needed them.

## Key people

Several members are worth knowing by name.

- Munnam Furzil works as a Solutions Architect and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Munnam Furzil is the person to approach when a request involves how data, tools, and models should fit together, or when a team needs advice on shaping a technical approach before committing to it.
- Pivoine Geltoett is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit and focuses on demand forecasting models. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil, which means forecasting work is supported by an architectural perspective from the start.
- Vadesis Gummenbel works as a Chief of Staff and is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. Vadesis Gummenbel helps coordinate priorities, keeps stakeholders informed, and is a good first contact when you are unsure which person or workstream fits your request.

Reporting lines in and around analytics work are meant to be simple. Pivoine Geltoett reports to Munnam Furzil. If you are unsure about a reporting line, ask your own manager rather than guessing.

## How to work with the unit

1. Start with the question. Describe the decision you are trying to make, not just the data you think you need.
2. Say what good looks like. Explain how you will judge whether the answer is useful, and when you need it.
3. Name an owner on your side. Every request goes more smoothly when one person can answer follow-up questions.
4. Be open to scoping. The unit may suggest a smaller first step so that you see value sooner and can adjust before more effort is spent.
5. Share the outcome. Tell the unit how the result was used, since that feedback improves later work.

Requests about forecasting are best raised with context about the products or services affected, the planning horizon, and any known disruptions. Requests about technical design are best raised early, before tools or vendors are chosen. Requests about priorities or timing can start with the Chief of Staff.

The unit aims to be easy to work with. Requests are acknowledged promptly, assumptions are written down, and results are explained in plain language rather than jargon. Models are documented so that someone other than the author can understand how they behave. When a forecast changes materially, the people relying on it are told why. Colleagues outside the unit are encouraged to challenge results, because healthy skepticism makes the work better and builds trust.

Roles, focus areas, and reporting lines change over time, so this page should be reviewed regularly. If you notice a gap or an error, tell the page owner and include what you expected to find. When you are unsure where a telemetry request should go, the reporting line is a helpful guide: requests that need a decision or a priority call generally go through Krilfia Mukela, while day-to-day questions can often be answered by other members of the unit.

A few practical tips for working with the unit:

- Describe the business question first, then the data you think you need. The unit can often suggest a better route to the answer.
- Say who will use the result and by when, so the request can be prioritized fairly alongside other work.
- Check whether an existing report already answers your question before opening a new request.
- Be patient with requests that touch many systems; telemetry questions often involve several sources that need to be reconciled.

**Engineering leadership**

Gonnom Gosmunza works as a Director of Engineering. Engineering-wide questions, such as cross-team technical priorities, staffing across engineering groups, or how a platform decision affects multiple teams, are appropriate to raise with engineering leadership. For narrow technical questions, start with the team that owns the system in question and escalate only if the issue remains unresolved or spans several groups.

**Upcoming launch: the Trebrula Beacon**

The Trebrula Beacon is scheduled to launch in Q1 FY27. Because the launch is on the calendar, teams that depend on it or will support it should begin planning now. Useful preparation includes:

- Reviewing which of your processes will change when the launch happens.
- Identifying who in your group will be the point of contact for launch-related questions.
- Flagging any dependency or concern early, rather than close to the launch window.
- Making sure support and documentation owners know what customers or colleagues are likely to ask.

Launch timing is a plan, not a guarantee, and plans can move. Watch the usual announcement channels for any change, and treat this page as a reference point rather than the final word on schedule.

**Current offering: the Feltarel Relay**

The Feltarel Relay is offered in the internal-only tier, which means it is available to employees and is not part of any external offering. The Feltarel Relay has about 1,800 active users. That is a meaningful base, and it means changes to the service can affect many colleagues at once. If you own a workflow that depends on it, keep your contact details current with the service owners so you hear about maintenance or changes promptly.

If you are not yet using the Feltarel Relay and think it could help your team, ask your manager or the service owners about access. Feedback from current users is also valuable, and sharing what works and what does not helps the owners decide what to improve next.

**Vendor renewal: Misginine Systems**

Misginine Systems is up for renewal in Q4 FY28. Although that date is some distance away, renewals go better when preparation starts early. Teams that rely on the vendor should consider the following:

- Collect honest feedback on how well the service has met your needs.
- Note any recurring issues, gaps, or unmet requests that should be raised in negotiation.
- Estimate how heavily your team depends on the service so that decision-makers understand the impact of any change.
- Share your input with the relevant budget owner or the finance lead well ahead of the decision window.

Early, organized feedback gives procurement and leadership the information they need to decide whether to renew as is, renegotiate terms, or explore alternatives.

**Where to go with questions**

- Telemetry and analytics: begin with the Dankenor Analytics Unit.
- Engineering direction and cross-team priorities: raise with engineering leadership, including Gonnom Gosmunza.
- Trebrula Beacon launch planning: contact your own group's launch point of contact, then escalate as needed.
- Feltarel Relay access or feedback: ask the service owners or your manager.
- Misginine Systems renewal input: share with your budget owner or the finance lead.

This page will be updated as plans change. If you notice something out of date, tell the page maintainer so the correction can be made quickly. Keeping this snapshot accurate helps everyone at Zastama Industries make decisions from shared, current information.

Restricted Access Working Notes: Budget Attribution and Architecture Review Coordination

**Summary**

This page is a working reference for the small group involved in the current architecture review and its associated budget tracking at Zastama Industries. It records who holds which responsibilities, how budget attribution is handled, and what the group expects to do next. It is not intended for company-wide circulation, so please do not forward it, paste excerpts into broader channels, or link it from open pages without checking with the page owner first.

**Purpose and Scope**

The group was formed to keep technical decisions and spending records aligned. In past cycles, design choices were sometimes made without a clear link to the budget line that would fund them, and finance later had to reconstruct the reasoning. This page exists to prevent that. It covers two things: the people and codes the group relies on day to day, and the working conventions we follow when a design decision has cost implications.

The page deliberately stays narrow. It does not describe vendor selection, customer commitments, or staffing plans. Those are handled elsewhere and are discussed only with the people who need to know.

**Key People and Budget Attribution**

Two individuals anchor most of the activity described here.

Nasgo Kesloren joined the company in 2020 and is one of the longer-tenured members of the group. Expenses and effort connected to the review are attributed to the budget code TU-1566-Y, which is the code that belongs to Nasgo Kesloren. When anyone submits a cost, a time allocation, or a purchase request tied to this work, that code should be used so that finance can reconcile entries without follow-up questions. If you are unsure whether an item belongs under this code, ask before submitting rather than correcting it afterward.

Liluan Nemlurel works as a Solutions Architect. She is the first point of contact for questions about how the proposed designs fit together, which constraints are firm, and which are negotiable. When a design question has a cost dimension, she is expected to raise it with the budget holder early, and the budget holder is expected to respond promptly so that decisions do not stall.

**Working Conventions**

- **Link decisions to budget.** Any design decision with a cost implication should name the budget code it will draw from in the notes that record the decision.
- **Keep records short and current.** A brief, accurate entry is more useful than a long one that nobody updates. Revise entries when the situation changes.
- **Escalate early.** If a cost estimate shifts materially, tell the finance lead and the budget holder as soon as you know, not at the next scheduled check-in.
- **Limit distribution.** Share material from this page only with colleagues who are already part of the review or who have a clear business reason to see it.

**Open Questions and Next Steps**

Several items remain open, and the group will work through them in its regular discussions:

1. Confirm with the finance lead that the attribution process described above matches current reconciliation practice.
2. Agree on a lightweight template for recording design decisions alongside their budget references.
3. Decide how often the group should review this page for accuracy, and who will own those reviews.
4. Clarify what, if anything, from this page can eventually be summarized for a wider audience without exposing restricted detail.

Until those items are settled, treat the conventions above as the working standard. Questions about the page itself should go to the page owner, and questions about budget treatment should go to the finance lead. If you notice anything out of date, correct it directly or flag it to the owner so that the record stays reliable for the next person who needs it. Zastama Industries expects restricted pages such as this one to be kept tidy and minimal.

Account Oversight and Staffing Alignment for the Gaskergur Harbor Engagement

TO: Account Leadership Group (Restricted Distribution)
FROM: Director of Client Operations
DATE: October 9, 2026
SUBJECT: Oversight, Reporting Lines, and Institutional Knowledge for the Gaskergur Harbor Engagement

This memo is intended only for the account leadership group and should not be forwarded beyond it. I am writing to confirm several points about how we are organizing oversight of the Gaskergur Harbor engagement, and to ask for your input before we finalize the arrangements. Some of this touches on staffing and reporting lines, which is why I have kept the distribution narrow.

First, the basics of the account. The Gaskergur Harbor has about 6,300 active users, which makes it one of the more demanding deployments we currently support from an operational standpoint. The scale of that user base affects how we think about support coverage, change windows, and the amount of coordination required whenever a modification is proposed. For the record and for anyone updating their working files, the contract governing this engagement is number HE-6807-Y for the Gaskergur Harbor. Please use that reference whenever you correspond with finance or legal about the agreement, and do not substitute informal shorthand in written exchanges.

Second, I want to clarify the reporting structure relevant to day-to-day delivery. Vadesis Gummenbel reports to Zosne Bramfa. I am restating this because a few recent threads suggested some uncertainty about who holds final decision authority when delivery questions arise. For routine operational matters, Vadesis Gummenbel should continue to work directly with the team and raise anything that needs escalation through Zosne Bramfa. I would ask that the rest of you route questions accordingly rather than going around that line, since doing so has previously produced duplicate instructions and avoidable confusion for the people doing the work.

Third, I want to acknowledge the value of institutional memory on this account. Liluan Nemlurel joined the company in 2016, and she has been a consistent source of context on how our practices have evolved over the years. When we discuss why certain procedures exist, or whether a proposed change repeats something we have tried before, her perspective has repeatedly saved us time. I would encourage you to involve Liluan Nemlurel early in any conversation that touches on historical decisions, particularly those that may affect the user base described above. Her tenure is not a substitute for documentation, and I would also like us to capture what she knows in writing so that it is not concentrated in one person.

With those points established, here is what I am asking of you over the coming weeks. Please review the reporting arrangement I described and tell me if any part of it conflicts with how your own groups currently operate. If it does, I would prefer to hear about it now rather than discover it during a delivery issue. Please also identify any open questions about the contract that you believe need a response from legal or finance, and send them to me in a single consolidated note rather than as separate messages. This will help me prioritize and avoid duplicated effort on the part of those functions.

In addition, I would like each of you to consider where our current support and coordination model might be strained by the size of the active user base. If you see gaps, such as unclear ownership of a recurring task, thin coverage during peak periods, or processes that rely on a single individual, please flag them. I am not looking for polished proposals at this stage. Short, candid observations are more useful, and I will compile them into a brief working document for discussion at our next leadership session.

Finally, a reminder about handling. Because this memo discusses reporting lines and individual contributors, please treat it as confidential and keep any discussion of it within the group. If you believe someone outside the distribution needs to see any part of it, speak with me first and I will decide how best to share the relevant content. Thank you for your attention and for your prompt responses.

Cross-Team Status Brief: Key Accounts, Projects, and Ownership

**Summary:** This page gives all employees a shared view of an important upcoming customer renewal, a project that needs attention, and a few ownership details that help people know whom to contact. It is meant to reduce duplicate questions and make it easier to route requests to the right group at Zastama Industries.

## Why this page exists

Over the past several planning cycles, employees have told us they are often unsure who owns a given tool, who leads a given effort, or which customer relationships are most time sensitive. This page collects a handful of those answers in one place. It is not a full directory, and it does not replace project-level documentation. Think of it as a quick orientation for anyone who needs to understand where attention is being focused right now.

## Customer renewal outlook

Nalzenett Labs is up for renewal in Q2 FY27. Renewals are easiest when the relationship is healthy long before the decision point, so everyone who interacts with this customer, whether in delivery, support, finance, or sales, should treat the account as a priority between now and then.

What this means in practice:

- Keep communication with the customer timely, clear, and honest.
- Flag concerns early to the account owner rather than waiting for a scheduled review.
- Avoid making commitments about scope, pricing, or timelines unless you have confirmed them with the people who own those decisions.
- If you are unsure whether a request is appropriate to take on, ask first.

## Project at risk

Project Vebamett has a services contract with Nalzenett Labs, which links the health of that project directly to the renewal conversation. Project Vebamett is currently at risk. That status does not assign blame to any individual or group. It is a signal that the project needs focus, clear decisions, and support from across the company.

If you are connected to the project, you can help by:

1. Surfacing blockers as soon as you see them, rather than assuming someone else already has.
2. Being specific about what you need, from whom, and by when.
3. Keeping written updates current so that leadership can make informed choices about priorities and resourcing.
4. Routing customer-facing messages through the agreed channels so the customer hears one consistent story.

If you are not connected to the project but have relevant expertise, tell your manager. Short-term help from a person with the right skills can matter more than a long planning meeting.

## Who leads and who owns what

The following assignments are useful to know when you are trying to find the right person or group:

- **Project leadership:** Berruan Zenresan leads Project Stebril. If your work touches that effort, she is the right person to coordinate with on priorities and sequencing.
- **Data retention:** Fallem Purraren focuses on data retention tooling. Questions about how retention capabilities are built or maintained should start there.
- **Identity and access:** The Gelgos Infrastructure Team is responsible for identity and access tooling. If you need help with access requests, permissions models, or related tooling issues, that group is your starting point.
- **Analytics:** Zosu Kistos is a member of the Dankenor Analytics Unit. For analytics questions, the unit is the appropriate home for your request, and Zosu Kistos is one of the people on it.

Please use the normal request channels when contacting these owners. Direct messages are fine for quick questions, but anything that needs tracking should go through the usual intake process so that work does not depend on one person's inbox.

## How to escalate

If something you see could affect the renewal or the at-risk project, tell your manager and the relevant owner above. Be factual, state what you observed, and note what you think the impact could be. If you are not sure whether something is significant, raise it anyway; it is better to have a quick conversation that turns out to be unnecessary than to miss an early warning.

## Keeping this page current

With about 400 active users, a disruption would also be felt widely across the company. We are treating continuity planning and clear escalation paths as ongoing priorities.

Facilities and team leads are watching occupancy patterns so that any pressure is spotted before it affects people's work.

3. *Concentrated operational knowledge.* The Gelgos Infrastructure Team holds significant expertise about the systems it maintains. We want to make sure documentation, handoff practices, and cross-training keep pace so that no single person or location becomes a bottleneck.

4. *Budget discipline.* The Fonathe Platform Group works within an annual budget of $4.1M. Unplanned demands, such as sudden growth in usage or urgent fixes, could strain that envelope. Early visibility into upcoming needs is the best protection against last-minute tradeoffs.

5. *Communication gaps.* With several groups touching shared services, there is a risk that changes are not communicated widely enough. Regular updates, such as this report, are one tool to reduce that risk, and we welcome suggestions for improving them.

**Next Steps**

- Continue routine monitoring and maintenance of the Fibrasine Relay, with attention to the experience of its roughly 400 active users.
